chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: ॐ धृतराष्ट्र उवाच । धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः । मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥ १ ॥
translation: Dhritarâshtra said: On the holy plain, on the field of Kuru, gathered together, eager for battle, what did they, O Sanjaya, my people and the Pândavas?

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा । आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ २ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: Having seen arrayed the army of the Pândavas, the Prince Duryodhana approached his teacher, and spake these words:

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् । व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥ ३ ॥
translation: "Behold this mighty host of the sons of Pându, O teacher, arrayed by the son of Drupada, thy wise disciple.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि । युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Heroes are these, mighty bowmen, to Bhîma and Arjuna equal in battle: Yuyudhâna, Virâta, and Drupada of the great car.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् । पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ॥ ५ ॥
translation: Drishtaketu, Chekitâna and the valiant King of Kâshi, Purujit and Kuntibhoja, and Shaivya, bull among men;

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् । सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Yudhâmanyu the strong, and Uttamaujas the brave; Saubhadra and the Draupadeyas, all of great cars.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम । नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥ ७ ॥
translation: Know further all those who are our chiefs, O best of the twice-born, the leaders of my army; these I name to thee for thy information:

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः । अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च ॥ ८ ॥
translation: Thou, Lord, and Bhîshma, and Karna and Kripa, conquering in battle; Ashvatthâmâ, Vikarna, and Saumadatti also;

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः । नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥ ९ ॥
translation: And many others, heroes, for my sake renouncing their lives, with divers weapons and missiles, and all well-skilled in war.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् । पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥ १० ॥
translation: Yet insufficient seems this army of ours, though marshalled by Bhîshma, while that army of theirs seems sufficient, though marshalled by Bhîma;

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः । भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ॥ ॥ ११ ॥
translation: Therefore in the rank and file let all, standing firmly in their respective divisions, guard Bhîshma, even all ye generals.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: तस्य सञ्जनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः । सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥ १२ ॥
translation: To enhearten him, the Ancient of the Kurus, the Grandsire, the glorious, blew his conch, sounding on high a lion's roar.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः । सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥ १३ ॥
translation: Then conches and kettledrums, tabors and drums and cowhorns, suddenly blared forth, and the sound was tumultuous.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ । माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥ १४ ॥
translation: Then, stationed in their great war-chariot, yoked to white horses, Mâdhava and the son of Pându blew their divine conches.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः । पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Pânchajanya by Hrishîkesha, and Devadatta by Dhananjaya. Vrikodara of terrible deeds blew his mighty conch, Paundra;

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥ १६ ॥
translation: The King Yudhishthira, the son of Kuntî, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva, Sughosha and Manipushpaka.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः । धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥ १७ ॥
translation: And Kâshya, of the great bow and Shikhandî, the mighty car-warrior, Drishtadyumna and Virâta and Sâtyaki, the unconquered.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते । सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥ १८ ॥
translation: Drupada and the Draupadeyas, O Lord of earth, and Saubhadra, the mighty-armed, on all sides their several conches blew.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् । नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् ॥ १९ ॥
translation: That tumultuous uproar rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarâshtra, filling the earth and sky with sound.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः । प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥ २० ॥
translation: Then, beholding the sons of Dhritarâshtra standing arrayed, and flight of missiles about to begin, he whose crest is an ape, the son of Pându, took up his bow,

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते । अर्जुन उवाच । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥ २१ ॥
translation: And spake this word to Hrishîkesha, O Lord of Earth: Arjuna said: In the midst, between the two armies, stay my chariot, O Achyuta,

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्‌धुकामानवस्थितान् । कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे ॥ २२ ॥
translation: That I may behold these standing, longing for battle, with whom I must strive in this outbreaking war,

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः । धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥ २३ ॥
translation: And gaze on those here gathered together ready to fight, desirous of pleasing in battle the evil-minded son of Dhritarâshtra.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥ २४ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: Thus addressed by Gudâkesha, Hrishîkesha, O Bhârata, having stayed that best of chariots in the midst, between the two armies,

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् । उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥ २५ ॥
translation: Over against Bhîshma, Drona and all the rulers of the world, said: "O Pârtha, behold these Kurus gathered together."

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितॄनथ पितामहान् । आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातॄन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ॥ २६ ॥
translation: Then saw Pârtha standing there, uncles and grandfathers, teachers, mother's brothers, cousins, sons and grandsons, comrades,

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि । तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Fathers-in-law and benefactors also in both armies; seeing all these kinsmen thus standing arrayed, Kaunteya,

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: कृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । अर्जुन उवाच । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥ २८ ॥
translation: Deeply moved to pity, thus uttered in sadness: Arjuna said: Seeing these my kinsmen, O Krishna, arrayed, eager to fight,

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ २९ ॥
translation: My limbs fail and my mouth is parched, my body quivers, and my hair stands on end,

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥ ३० ॥
translation: Gândîva slips from my hand, and my skin burns all over, I am not able to stand, my mind is whirling,

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव । न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥ ३१ ॥
translation: And I see adverse omens, O Keshava. Nor do I foresee any advantage from slaying kinsmen in battle.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च । किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥ ३२ ॥
translation: For I desire not victory, O Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures; what is kingdom to us, O Govinda, what enjoyment or even life?

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च । त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥ ३३ ॥
translation: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures, they stand here in battle, abandoning life and riches—

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः । मातुलाः श्वशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥ ३४ ॥
translation: Teachers, fathers, sons, as well as grandfathers, mother's brothers, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन । अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥ ३५ ॥
translation: These I do not wish to kill, though myself slain, O Madhusûdana, even for the sake of the kingship of the three worlds; how then for earth?

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन । पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥ ३६ ॥
translation: Slaying these sons of Dhritarâshtra, what pleasure can be ours, O Janârdana? Killing these desperadoes, sin will but take hold of us.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् । स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥ ३७ ॥
translation: Therefore we should not kill the sons of Dhritarâshtra, our relatives; for how, killing our kinsmen, may we be happy, O Mâdhava?

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥ ३८ ॥
translation: Although these, with intelligence overpowered by greed, see no guilt in the destruction of a family, no crime in hostility to friends,

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥ ३९ ॥
translation: Why should not we learn to turn away from such a sin, O Janârdana, who see the evils in the destruction of a family?

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः । धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥ ४० ॥
translation: In the destruction of a family the immemorial family traditions perish; in the perishing of tradition, lawlessness overcomes the whole family;

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः । स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥ ४१ ॥
translation: Owing to predominance of lawlessness, O Krishna, the women of the family become corrupt; women corrupted, O Vârshneya, there ariseth caste confusion;

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च । पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥ ४२ ॥
translation: This confusion draggeth to hell the slayers of the family, and the family; for their ancestors fall, deprived of rice-balls and libations.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः । उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥ ४३ ॥
translation: By these caste-confusing misdeeds of the slayers of the family, the everlasting caste customs and family customs are abolished.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन । नरके नियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम ॥ ४४ ॥
translation: The abode of the men whose family customs are extinguished, O Janârdana, is everlastingly in hell. Thus have we heard.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् । यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ॥ ४५ ॥
translation: Alas! in committing a great sin are we engaged, we who are endeavouring to kill our kindred from greed of the pleasures of kingship.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः । धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥ ४६ ॥
translation: If the sons of Dhritarâshtra, weapon in hand, should slay me, unresisting, unarmed, in the battle, that would for me be the better.

chapterSummary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । एवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः सङ्ख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥ ४७ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: Having thus spoken on the battle-field, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, casting away his bow and arrow, his mind overborne by grief.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । तं तथा कृपयाऽऽविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् । विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥ १ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: To him thus with pity overcome, with smarting brimming eyes, despondent, Madhusûdana spake these words:

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् । अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥ २ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Whence hath this dejection befallen thee in this perilous strait, ignoble, heaven-closing, infamous, O Arjuna?

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: क्लैव्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते । क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ट परन्तप ॥ ३ ॥
translation: Yield not to impotence, O Partha! it doth not befit thee. Shake off this paltry faint-heartedness! Stand up, Parantapa!

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । कथं भीष्ममहं सङ्ख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन । इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: How, O Madhusûdana, shall I attack Bhîshma and Drona with arrows in battle, they who are worthy of reverence, O slayer of foes?

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान् श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके । हत्वाऽर्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव भुञ्जीय भोगान्रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥ ५ ॥
translation: Better in this world to eat even the beggar's crust than to slay these most noble Gurus. Slaying these Gurus, our well-wishers, I should taste of blood-besprinkled feasts.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः । यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषाम: तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Nor know I which for us be the better, that we conquer them or they conquer us—these, whom having slain we should not care to live, even these arrayed against us, the sons of Dhritarâshtra.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसम्मूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥ ७ ॥
translation: My heart is weighed down with the vice of faintness; my mind is confused as to duty. I ask thee which may be the better—that tell me decisively. I am thy disciple, suppliant to Thee; teach me.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥ ८ ॥
translation: For I see not that it would drive away this anguish that withers up my senses, if I should attain unrivalled monarchy on earth, or even the sovereignty of the Shining Ones.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तपः । न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥ ९ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: Gudâkesha, conqueror of his foes, having thus addressed Hrishîkesha and said to Govinda, "I will not fight!", became silent.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥ १० ॥
translation: Then Hrishîkesha, smiling, as it were, O Bhârata, spake these words to him, despondent, in the midst of the two armies:

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.

translation: The Blessed Lord said: Thou grievest for those that should not be grieved for, yet speakest words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः । न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥ १२ ॥
translation: Nor at any time verily was I not, nor thou, nor these princes of men, nor verily shall we ever cease to be, hereafter.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥ १३ ॥
translation: As the dweller in the body experienceth in the body childhood, youth, old age, so passeth he on to another body; the steadfast one grieveth not thereat.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः । आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥ १४ ॥
translation: The contacts of matter, O son of Kuntî, giving cold and heat, pleasure and pain, they come and go, impermanent; endure them bravely, O Bhârata.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥ १५ ॥
translation: The man whom these torment not, O chief of men, balanced in pain and pleasure, steadfast, he is fitted for immortality.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः । उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥ १६ ॥
translation: The unreal hath no being; the real never ceaseth to be; the truth about both hath been perceived by the seers of the essence of things.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥ १७ ॥
translation: Know That to be indestructible by whom all this is pervaded. Nor can any work the destruction of that imperishable One.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः । अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥ १८ ॥
translation: These bodies of the embodied One, who is eternal, indestructible and immeasurable, are known as finite. Therefore fight, O Bhârata.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् । उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥ १९ ॥
translation: He who regardeth this as a slayer, and he who thinketh he is slain, both of them are ignorant. He slayeth not, nor is he slain.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः । अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥ २० ॥
translation: He is not born, nor doth he die; nor having been, ceaseth he any more to be; unborn, perpetual, eternal and ancient, he is not slain when the body is slaughtered.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: वेदाऽविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् । कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥ २१ ॥
translation: Who knoweth him indestructible, perpetual, unborn, undiminishing, how can that man slay, O Pârtha, or cause to be slain?

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि । तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥ २२ ॥
translation: As a man, casting off worn-out garments, taketh new ones, so the dweller in the body, casting off worn-out bodies, entereth into others that are new.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः । न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥ २३ ॥
translation: Weapons cleave him not, nor fire burneth him, nor waters wet him, nor wind drieth him away.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च । नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥ २४ ॥
translation: Uncleavable he, incombustible he, and indeed neither to be wetted nor dried away; perpetual, all-pervasive, stable, immovable, ancient.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते । तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २५ ॥
translation: Unmanifest, unthinkable, immutable, he is called; therefore knowing him as such, thou shouldst not grieve.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् । तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैनं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २६ ॥
translation: Or if thou thinkest of him as being constantly born and constantly dying, even then, O mighty-armed, thou shouldst not grieve.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.

translation: For certain is death for the born, and certain is birth for the dead; therefore over the inevitable thou shouldst not grieve.

translation: Beings are unmanifest in their origin, manifest in their midmost state, O Bhârata, unmanifest likewise are they in dissolution. What room then for lamentation?

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.

translation: As marvellous one regardeth him; as marvellous another speaketh thereof; as marvellous another heareth thereof; yet having heard none indeed understandeth.

translation: This dweller in the body of everyone is ever invulnerable, O Bhârata; therefore thou shouldst not grieve for any creature.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.

translation: Further, looking to thine own duty thou shouldst not tremble; for there is nothing more welcome to a Kshattriya than righteous war.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.

translation: Happy the Kshattriyas, O Pârtha, who obtain such a fight, offered unsought as an open door to heaven.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.

translation: But if thou wilt not carry on this righteous warfare, then casting away thine own duty and thine honour, thou wilt incur sin.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.

translation: Men will recount thy perpetual dishonour, and, to one highly esteemed, dishonour exceedeth death.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः । येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥ ३५ ॥
translation: The great car-warriors will think thee fled from the battle from fear, and thou, that wast highly thought of by them, wilt be lightly held.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः । निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥ ३६ ॥
translation: Many unseemly words will be spoken by thine enemies, slandering thy strength; what more painful than that?

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् । तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥ ३७ ॥
translation: Slain, thou wilt obtain heaven; victorious, thou wilt enjoy the earth; therefore stand up, O son of Kuntî, resolute to fight.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३८ ॥
translation: Taking as equal pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, gird thee for the battle; thus thou shalt not incur sin.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: एषा तेऽभिहिता साङ्ख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु । बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥ ३९ ॥
translation: This teaching set forth to thee is in accordance with the Sâñkhya; hear it now according to the Yoga, imbued with which teaching, O Pârtha, thou shalt cast away the bonds of action.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥ ४० ॥
translation: In this there is no loss of effort, nor is there transgression. Even a little of this knowledge protects from great fear.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: व्ययसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन । बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥ ४१ ॥
translation: The determinate Reason is but one-pointed, O joy of the Kurus; many-branched and endless are the thoughts of the irresolute.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः । वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥ ४२ ॥
translation: Flowery speech is uttered by the foolish, rejoicing in the letter of the Vedas, O Pârtha, saying: "There is naught but this";

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.

translation: With desire for self, with heaven for goal, they offer birth as the fruit of action, and prescribe many and various ceremonies for the attainment of pleasure and lordship.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.

translation: For them who cling to pleasure and lordship, whose minds are captivated by such teaching, is not designed this determinate Reason, on contemplation steadily bent.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन । निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥ ४५ ॥
translation: The Vedas deal with the three attributes; be thou above these three attributes, O Arjuna; beyond the pairs of opposites, ever steadfast in purity, careless of possessions, full of the Self.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके । तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥ ४६ ॥
translation: All the Vedas are as useful to an enlightened Brâhmana as is a tank in a place covered all over with water.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ ४७ ॥
translation: Thy business is with the action only, never with its fruits; so let not the fruit of action be thy motive, nor be thou to inaction attached.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥ ४८ ॥
translation: Perform action, O Dhananjaya, dwelling in union with the divine, renouncing attachments and balanced evenly in success and failure: equilibrium is called yoga.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय । बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥ ४९ ॥
translation: Far lower than the Yoga of Discrimination is action, O Dhananjaya. Take thou refuge in the Pure Reason; pitiable are they who work for fruit.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते । तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥ ५० ॥
translation: United to the Pure Reason one abandoneth here both good and evil deeds; therefore cleave thou to yoga; yoga is skill in action.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः । जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥ ५१ ॥
translation: The Sages, united to the Pure Reason, renounce the fruit which action yieldeth, and, liberated from the bonds of birth, they go to the blissful seat.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति । तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥ ५२ ॥
translation: When thy mind shall escape from this tangle of delusion, then thou shalt rise to indifference as to what has been heard and shall be heard.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला । समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ५३ ॥
translation: When thy mind, bewildered by the Scriptures, shall stand immovable, fixed in contemplation, then shalt thou attain unto yoga.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव । स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥ ५४ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: What the mark, of him who is stable of mind, steadfast in contemplation, O Keshava? How doth the stable-minded talk, how doth he sit, how walk?

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् । आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥ ५५ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: When a man abandoneth, O Pârtha, all the desires of the heart, and is satisfied in the Self by the Self, then is he called stable in mind.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः । वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥ ५६ ॥
translation: He whose mind is free from anxiety amid pains, indifferent amid pleasures, loosed from passion, fear and anger, is called a sage of stable mind.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् । नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५७ ॥
translation: He who on every side is without attachments, whatever hap of fair and foul, who neither likes nor dislikes, of such a one the understanding is well poised.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५८ ॥
translation: When, again, as a tortoise draws in on all sides its limbs, he withdraws his senses from the objects of sense, then is his understanding well poised.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः । रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥ ५९ ॥
translation: The objects of sense, but not the relish for them, turn away from an abstemious dweller in the body; and even relish turneth away from him after the Supreme is seen.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥ ६० ॥
translation: O son of Kuntî, the excited senses of even a wise man, though he be striving, impetuously carry away his mind.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः । वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६१ ॥
translation: Having restrained them all, he should sit harmonised, I his supreme goal; for, whose senses are mastered, of him the understanding is well poised.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥ ६२ ॥
translation: Man, musing on the objects of sense, conceiveth an attachment to these; from attachment ariseth desire; from desire anger cometh forth;

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥ ६३ ॥
translation: From anger proceedeth delusion; from delusion confused memory; from confused memory the destruction of Reason; from destruction of Reason he perishes.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तुं विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् । आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥ ६४ ॥
translation: But the disciplined self, moving among sense-objects with senses free from attraction and repulsion, mastered by the Self, goeth to peace.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते । प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥ ६५ ॥
translation: In that Peace the extinction of all pains ariseth for him, for of him whose heart is peaceful the Reason soon attaineth equilibrium.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना । न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥ ६६ ॥
translation: There is no Pure Reason for the non-harmonised, nor for the non-harmonised is there concentration; for him without concentration there is no peace, and for the unpeaceful how can there be happiness?

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनु विधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥ ६७ ॥
translation: Such of the roving senses as the mind yieldeth to, that hurries away the understanding, just as the gale hurries away a ship upon the waters.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६८ ॥
translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed, whose senses are all completely restrained from the objects of sense, of him the understanding is well poised.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥ ६९ ॥
translation: That which is the night of all beings, for the disciplined man is the time of waking; when other beings are waking, then is it night for the sage who seeth.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् । तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥ ७० ॥
translation: He attaineth Peace, into whom all desires flow as rivers flow into the ocean, which is filled with water, but remaineth unmoved—not he who desireth desires.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥ ७१ ॥
translation: Whoso forsaketh all desires and goeth onwards free from yearnings, selfless and without egoism—he goeth to Peace.

chapterSummary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति । स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्म निर्वाणमृच्छति ॥ ७२ ॥
translation: This is the Eternal state, O son of Prithâ. Having attained thereto, none is bewildered. Who, even at the death-hour, is established therein, he goeth to the Nirvâna of the Eternal.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन । तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥ १ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: If it be thought by Thee that knowledge is superior to action, O Janârdana, why dost Thou, O Keshava, enjoin on me this terrible action?

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥ २ ॥
translation: With these perplexing words Thou only confusest my understanding; therefore tell me with certainty the one way by which I may reach bliss.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयाऽनघ । ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥ ३ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: In this world there is a twofold path, as I before said, O sinless one: that of yoga by knowledge, of the Sâñkhyas; and that of yoga by action, of the Yogis.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते । न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Man winneth not freedom from action by abstaining from activity, nor by mere renunciation doth he rise to perfection.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् । कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥ ५ ॥
translation: Nor can anyone, even for an instant, remain really actionless; for helplessly is everyone driven to action by the qualities born of nature.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् । इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Who sitteth, controlling the organs of action, but dwelling in his mind on the objects of the senses, that bewildered man is called a hypocrite.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन । कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥ ७ ॥
translation: But who, controlling the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, with the organs of action without attachment, performeth yoga by action, he is worthy.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्राऽपि च ते न प्रसिध्येदकर्मणः ॥ ८ ॥
translation: Perform thou right action, for, action is superior to inaction, and, inactive, even the maintenance of thy body would not be possible.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः । तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ॥ ९ ॥
translation: The world is bound by action, unless performed for the sake of sacrifice; for that sake, free from attachment, O son of Kuntî, perform thou action.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः । अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥ १० ॥
translation: Having in ancient times emanated mankind together with sacrifice, the Lord of emanation said: "By this shall ye propagate; be this to you the giver of desire;

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः । परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥ ११ ॥
translation: "With this nourish ye the Shining Ones, and may the Shining Ones nourish you; thus nourishing one another ye shall reap the supremest good.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः । तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥ १२ ॥
translation: "For, nourished by sacrifice, the Shining Ones shall bestow on you the enjoyments you desire." A thief verily is he who enjoyeth what is given by Them without returning Them aught.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः । भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥ १३ ॥
translation: The righteous, who eat the remains of the sacrifice, are freed from all sins; but the impious, who dress food for their own sakes, they verily eat sin.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसंभवः । यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥ १४ ॥
translation: From food creatures become; from rain is the production of food; rain proceedeth from sacrifice; sacrifice ariseth out of action.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माऽक्षरसमुद्भवम् । तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Know thou that from Brahma action groweth, and Brahma from the Imperishable cometh. Therefore the Eternal, the all-permeating, is ever present in sacrifice.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः । अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥ १६ ॥
translation: He who on earth doth not follow the wheel thus revolving, sinful of life and rejoicing in the senses, he, O son of Pritha, liveth in vain.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥ १७ ॥
translation: But the man who rejoiceth in the Self, with the Self is satisfied, and is content in the Self, for him verily there is nothing to do;

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन । न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥ १८ ॥
translation: For him there is no interest in things done, in this world, nor any in things not done, nor doth any object of his depend on any being.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥ १९ ॥
translation: Therefore, without attachment, constantly perform action which is duty, for, by performing action without attachment, man verily reacheth the Supreme.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः । लोकसङ्ग्रहमेवापि सम्पश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥ २० ॥
translation: Janaka and others indeed attained to perfection by action: then having an eye to the welfare of he world also, thou shouldst perform action.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥ २१ ॥
translation: Whatsoever a great man doeth, that other men also do; the standard he setteth up, by that the people go.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन । नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥ २२ ॥
translation: There is nothing in the three worlds, O Pârtha, that should be done by Me, nor anything unattained that might be attained; yet I mingle in action.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥ २३ ॥
translation: For if I mingled not ever in action unwearied, men all around would follow My path, O son of Prithâ.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् । सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥ २४ ॥
translation: These worlds would fall into ruin, if I did not perform action; I should be the author of confusion of castes, and should destroy these creatures.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत । कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथाऽसक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसङ्ग्रहम् ॥ २५ ॥
translation: As the ignorant act from attachment to action, O Bhârata, so should the wise act without attachment, desiring the welfare of the world.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् । जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ॥ २६ ॥
translation: Let no wise man unsettle the mind of ignorant people attached to action; but acting in harmony with Me let him render all action attractive.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः । अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥ २७ ॥
translation: All actions are wrought by the qualities of nature only. The self, deluded by egoism, thinketh: "I am the doer."

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः । गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥ २८ ॥
translation: But he, O mighty-armed, who knoweth the essence of the divisions of the qualities and functions, holding that "the qualities move amid the qualities," is not attached.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु । तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥ २९ ॥
translation: Those deluded by the qualities of nature are attached to the functions of the qualities. The man of perfect knowledge should not unsettle the foolish whose knowledge is imperfect.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याऽध्यात्मचेतसा । निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥ ३० ॥
translation: Surrendering all actions to Me, with thy thoughts resting on the supreme Self, from hope and egoism freed, and of mental fever cured, engage in battle.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः । श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥ ३१ ॥
translation: Who abide ever in this teaching of Mine full of faith and free from caviling, they too are released from actions.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
