sanskrit: ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् । सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥ ३२ ॥
translation: Who carp at My teaching and act not thereon, senseless, deluded in all knowledge, know thou these mindless ones as fated to be destroyed.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि । प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥ ३३ ॥
translation: Even the man of knowledge behaves in conformity with his own nature; beings follow nature; what shall restraint avail?

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ । तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥ ३४ ॥
translation: Affection and aversion for the objects of sense abide in the senses; let none come under the dominion of these two; they are obstructors of the path.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥ ३५ ॥
translation: Better one's own duty, though destitute of merit, than the duty of another, well discharged. Better death in the discharge of one's own duty; the duty of another is full of danger.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥ ३६ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: But dragged on by what does a man commit sin, reluctantly indeed, O Varshneya, as it were by force constrained?

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥ ३७ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is wrath, begotten by the quality of motion; all-consuming, all-polluting, know thou this as our foe here on earth.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: धूमेनाऽव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥ ३८ ॥
translation: As a flame is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dust, as an embryo is wrapped by the amnion, so This is enveloped by it.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा । कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥ ३९ ॥
translation: Enveloped is wisdom by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, which is insatiable as a flame.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते । एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥ ४० ॥
translation: The senses, the mind and the Reason are said to be its seat; by these enveloping wisdom, it bewilders the dweller in the body.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ । पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥ ४१ ॥
translation: Therefore, O best of the Bhâratas, mastering first the senses, do thou slay this thing of sin, destructive of wisdom and knowledge.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥ ४२ ॥
translation: It is said that the senses are great; greater than the senses is the mind: greater than the mind is the Reason; but what is greater than the Reason, is He. (42

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.
sanskrit: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना । जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥ ४३ ॥
translation: Thus understanding Him as greater than the Reason, restraining the self by the Self, slay thou, O mighty-armed, the enemy in the form of desire, difficult to overcome.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् । विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥ १ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: This imperishable yoga I declared to Vivasvân; Vivasvân taught it to Manu; Manu to Ikshvâku told it.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः । स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥ २ ॥
translation: This, handed on down the line, the King-Sages knew. This yoga by great efflux of time decayed in the world, O Parantapa.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: स एवाऽयं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः । भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥ ३ ॥
translation: This same ancient yoga hath been to-day declared to thee by Me, for thou art My devotee and My friend; it is the supreme Secret.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः । कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Later was Thy birth, earlier the birth of Vivasvân; how then am I to understand that Thou declaredst it in the beginning?

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन । तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥ ५ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Many births have been left behind by Me and by thee, O Arjuna. I know them all, but thou knowest not thine, O Parantapa.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् । प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्टाय सम्भवाम्यात्ममायया ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Though unborn, the imperishable Self, and also the Lord of all beings, brooding over nature which is Mine own, yet I am born through My own Power.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत । अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥ ७ ॥
translation: Whenever there is decay of righteousness, O Bhârata, and there is exaltation of unrighteousness, then I Myself come forth;

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥ ८ ॥
translation: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil-doers, for the sake of firmly establishing righteousness, I am born from age to age.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः । त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥ ९ ॥
translation: He who thus knoweth My divine birth and action, in its essence, having abandoned the body, cometh not to birth again, but cometh unto Me, O Arjuna.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः । बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥ १० ॥
translation: Freed from passion, fear and anger, filled with Me, taking refuge in Me, purified in the fire of wisdom, many have entered into My Being.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥ ११ ॥
translation: However men approach Me, even so do I welcome them, for the path men take from every side is Mine, O Pârtha.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः । क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥ १२ ॥
translation: They who long after success in action on earth worship the Shining Ones; for in brief space verily, in this world of men, success is born of action.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः । तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥ १३ ॥
translation: The four castes were emanated by Me, by the different distribution of qualities and actions; know Me to be the author of them, though the actionless and inexhaustible.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा । इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बद्ध्यते ॥ १४ ॥
translation: Nor do actions affect Me, nor is the fruit of action desired by Me. He who thus knoweth Me is not bound by actions.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः । कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Having thus known, our forefathers, ever seeking liberation, performed action; therefore do thou also perform action, as did our forefathers in the olden time.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः । तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥ १६ ॥
translation: "What is action, what inaction"? Even the wise are herein perplexed. Therefore I will declare to thee the action by knowing which thou shalt be loosed from evil.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः । अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥ १७ ॥
translation: It is needful to discriminate action, to discriminate unlawful action, and to discriminate inaction; mysterious is the path of action.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः । स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥ १८ ॥
translation: He who seeth inaction in action, and action in inaction, he is wise among men, he is harmonious, even while performing all action.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः । ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥ १९ ॥
translation: Whose works are all free from the moulding of desire, whose actions are burned up by the fire of wisdom, him the wise have called a Sage.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः । कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥ २० ॥
translation: Having abandoned attachment to the fruit of action, always content, nowhere seeking refuge, he is not doing anything, although doing actions.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः । शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ २१ ॥
translation: Hoping for naught, his mind and self controlled, having abandoned all greed, performing action by the body alone, he doth not commit sin.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वाऽपि न निबध्यते ॥ २२ ॥
translation: Content with whatsoever he obtaineth without effort, free from the pairs of opposites, without envy, balanced in success and failure, though acting he is not bound.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः । यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥ २३ ॥
translation: Of one with attachment dead, harmonious, with his thoughts established in wisdom, his works sacrifices, all action melts away.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् । ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥ २४ ॥
translation: The Eternal the oblation, the Eternal the clarified butter, are offered in the Eternal the fire by the Eternal; unto the Eternal verily shall he go who in his action meditateth wholly upon the Eternal.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते । ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥ २५ ॥
translation: Some Yogis offer up sacrifice to the Shining Ones; others sacrifice only by pouring sacrifice into the fire of the Eternal;

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति । शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥ २६ ॥
translation: Some pour as sacrifice hearing and the other senses into the fires of restraint; some pour sound and the other objects of sense into the fires of the senses as sacrifice;

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे । आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Others again into the wisdom-kindled fire of union attained by self-control, pour as sacrifice all the functions of the senses and the functions of life;

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथाऽपरे । स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः ॥ २८ ॥
translation: Yet others the sacrifice of wealth, the sacrifice of austerity, the sacrifice of yoga, the sacrifice of silent reading and wisdom, men concentrated and of effectual vows;

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे । प्राणापानगती रुध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥ २९ ॥
translation: Yet others pour as sacrifice the outgoing breath in the incoming, and the incoming in the outgoing, restraining the flow of the outgoing and incoming breaths, solely absorbed in the control of breathing.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति । सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः ॥ ३० ॥
translation: Others regular in food, pour as sacrifice their life-breaths in life-breaths. All these are knowers of sacrifice, and by sacrifice have destroyed their sins.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् । नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥ ३१ ॥
translation: The eaters of the life-giving remains of sacrifice go to the changeless Eternal. This world is not for the non-sacrificer, much less the other, O best of the Kurus.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे । कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥ ३२ ॥
translation: Many and various sacrifices are thus spread out before the Eternal. Know thou that all these are born of action, and thus knowing thou shalt be free.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप । सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥ ३३ ॥
translation: Better than the sacrifice of any objects is the sacrifice of wisdom, O Parantapa. All actions in their entirety, O Pârtha, culminate in wisdom.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥ ३४ ॥
translation: Learn thou this by discipleship, by investigation, and by service. The wise, the seers of the essence of things, will instruct thee in wisdom.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव । येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि ॥ ३५ ॥
translation: And having known this, thou shalt not again fall into this confusion, O Pândava; for by this thou wilt see all beings without exception in the Self, and thus in Me.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥ ३६ ॥
translation: Even if thou art the most sinful of all sinners, yet shalt thou cross over all sin by the raft of wisdom.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन । ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥ ३७ ॥
translation: As the burning fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so doth the fire of wisdom reduce all actions to ashes.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते । तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥ ३८ ॥
translation: Verily there is no purifier in this world like wisdom; he that is perfected in yoga finds it in the Self in due season.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः । ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ३९ ॥
translation: The man who is full of faith obtaineth wisdom, and he also who hath mastery over his senses; and, having obtained wisdom, he goeth swiftly to the supreme Peace.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति । नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥ ४० ॥
translation: But the ignorant, faithless, doubting self goeth to destruction; nor this world, nor that beyond, nor happiness, is there for the doubting self.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसञ्छिन्नसंशयम् । आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥ ४१ ॥
translation: He who hath renounced actions by yoga, who hath cloven asunder doubt by wisdom, who is ruled by the Self, actions do not bind him, O Dhananjaya.

chapterTitle: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapterSummary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.
sanskrit: तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः । छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥ ४२ ॥
translation: Therefore, with the sword of the wisdom of the Self cleaving asunder this ignorance-born doubt dwelling in thy heart, be established in yoga. Stand up, O Bhârata.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि । यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्चितम् ॥ १ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Renunciation of actions Thou praisest, O Krishna, and then also yoga. Of the two which one is the better? That tell me conclusively.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ । तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥ २ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Renunciation and yoga by action both lead to the highest bliss; of the two, yoga by action is verily better than renunciation of action.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति । निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
translation: He should be known as a perpetual ascetic, who neither hateth nor desireth; free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed, he is easily set free from bondage.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: साङ्ख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः । एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Children, not sages, speak of the Sânkhya and the Yoga as different; he who is duly established in one obtaineth the fruits of both.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते । एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥ ५ ॥
translation: That place which is gained by the Sânkhyas is reached by the Yogîs also. He seeth, who seeth that the Sânkhya and the Yoga are one.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः । योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म न चिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ६ ॥
translation: But without yoga, O mighty-armed, renunciation is hard to attain to; the yoga-harmonised Muni swiftly goeth to the Eternal.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः । सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥ ७ ॥
translation: He who is harmonised by yoga, the self purified, Self-ruled, the senses subdued, whose Self is the Self of all beings, although acting he is not affected.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: नैव किञ्चित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् । पश्यन्शृण्वन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्श्वसन्स्वपन् ॥ ८ ॥
translation: "I do not anything," should think the harmonised one, who knoweth the essence of things; seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन् ॥ ९ ॥
translation: Speaking, giving, grasping, opening and closing the eyes, he holdeth: "The senses move among the objects of the senses."

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः । लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥ १० ॥
translation: He who acteth, placing all actions in the Eternal, abandoning attachment, is unaffected by sin as a lotus leaf by the waters.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि । योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये ॥ ११ ॥
translation: Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform action only by the body, by the mind, by the Reason, and even by the senses, for the purification of the self.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥ १२ ॥
translation: The harmonised man, having abandoned the fruit of action, attaineth to the eternal Peace; the non-harmonised, impelled by desire, attached to fruit, are bound.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी । नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् ॥ १३ ॥
translation: Mentally renouncing all actions, the sovereign dweller in the body resteth serenely in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing to act.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः । न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते ॥ १४ ॥
translation: The Lord of the world produceth not the idea of agency, nor actions, nor the union together of action and its fruit; nature, however, manifesteth.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः । अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥ १५ ॥
translation: The Lord accepteth neither the evil-doing nor yet the well-doing of any. Wisdom is enveloped by unwisdom; therewith mortals are deluded.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः । तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् ॥ १६ ॥
translation: Verily, in whom unwisdom is destroyed by the wisdom of the Self, in them wisdom, shining as the sun, reveals the Supreme.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः । गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः ॥ १७ ॥
translation: Thinking on That, merged in That, established in That, solely devoted to That, they go whence there is no return, their sins dispelled by wisdom.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: विद्याविनयसम्पन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि । शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥ १८ ॥
translation: Sages look equally on a Brâhmana adorned with learning and humility, a cow, an elephant, and even a dog and an outcaste.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः । निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥ १९ ॥
translation: Even here on earth everything is overcome by those whose mind remains balanced; the Eternal is incorruptible and balanced; therefore they are established in the Eternal.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसंमूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥ २० ॥
translation: With Reason firm, unperplexed, the knower of the Eternal established in the Eternal, neither rejoiceth on obtaining what is pleasant, nor sorroweth on obtaining what is unpleasant.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥ २१ ॥
translation: He, whose self is unattached to external contacts and findeth joy in the Self, having the self harmonised with the Eternal by yoga, enjoys imperishable bliss.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते । आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥ २२ ॥
translation: The delights that are contact-born, they are verily wombs of pain, for they have beginning and ending, O Kaunteya; not in them may rejoice the wise.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक् शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥ २३ ॥
translation: He who is able to endure here on earth, ere he be liberated from the body, the force born from desire and passion, he is harmonised, he is a happy man.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥ २४ ॥
translation: He who is happy within, who rejoiceth within, who is illuminated within, that Yogî, becoming the Eternal, goeth to the Peace of the Eternal.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः । छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥ २५ ॥
translation: Rishis, their sins destroyed, their duality removed, their selves controlled, intent upon the welfare of all beings, obtain the Peace of the Eternal.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम् । अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम् ॥ २६ ॥
translation: The Peace of the Eternal lies near to those who know themselves, who are disjoined from desire and passion, subdued in nature, of subdued thoughts.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः । प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Having external contacts excluded, and with gaze fixed between the eyebrows; having made equal the outgoing and ingoing breaths moving within the nostrils;

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः । विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥ २८ ॥
translation: With senses, mind, and Reason ever controlled, solely pursuing liberation, the Sage, having for ever cast away desire, fear and passion, verily is liberated.

chapterSummary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.
sanskrit: भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् । सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥ २९ ॥
translation: Having known Me, as the Enjoyer of sacrifice and of austerity, the mighty Ruler of all the worlds, and the Lover of all beings, he goeth to Peace.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥ १ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: He that performeth such action as his duty, independently of the fruit of action, he is an ascetic, he is a Yogî, not he that is without fire, and without rites.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव । न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥ २ ॥
translation: That which is called renunciation, know thou that as yoga, O Pândava; nor doth any one become a Yogî with the formative will unrenounced.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते । योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
translation: For a Sage who is seeking Yoga, action is called the means; for the same Sage, when he is enthroned in yoga, serenity is called the means.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते । सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥ ४ ॥
translation: When a man feeleth no attachment either for the objects of sense or for actions, renouncing the formative will, then, he is said to be enthroned in yoga.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥ ५ ॥
translation: Let him raise the self by the Self and not let the self become depressed; for verily is the Self the friend of the self, and also the Self the self's enemy;

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः । अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥ ६ ॥
translation: The Self is the friend of the self of him in whom the self by the Self is vanquished; but to the unsubdued self the Self verily becometh hostile as an enemy.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥ ७ ॥
translation: The higher Self of him who is Self-controlled and peaceful is uniform in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honour and dishonour.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः । युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥ ८ ॥
translation: The Yogî who is satisfied with wisdom and knowledge, unwavering, whose senses are subdued, to whom a lump of earth, a stone and gold are the same, is said to be harmonised.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु । साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥ ९ ॥
translation: He who regards impartially lovers, friends, and foes, strangers, neutrals, foreigners and relatives, also the righteous and unrighteous, he excelleth.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः । एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥ १० ॥
translation: Let the Yogî constantly engage himself in yoga, remaining in a secret place by himself, with thought and self subdued, free from hope and greed.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः । नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चेलाजिनकुशोत्तरम् ॥ ११ ॥
translation: In a pure place, established on a fixed seat of his own, neither very much raised nor very low, made of a cloth, a black antelope skin, and kusha grass, one over the other;

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः । उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये ॥ १२ ॥
translation: There, having made the mind one-pointed, with thought and the functions of the senses subdued, steady on his seat, he should practise yoga for the purification of the self.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः । संप्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥ १३ ॥
translation: Holding the body, head and neck erect, immovably steady, looking fixedly at the point of the nose, with unseeing gaze,

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः । मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥ १४ ॥
translation: The self serene, fearless, firm in the vow of the Brahmachâri, the mind controlled, thinking on Me, harmonised, let him sit aspiring after Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः । शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥ १५ ॥
translation: The Yogî ever united thus with the Self, with the mind controlled, goeth to Peace, to the supreme Bliss that abideth in Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥ १६ ॥
translation: Verily yoga is not for him who eateth too much, nor who abstaineth to excess, nor who is too much addicted to sleep, nor even to wakefulness, O Arjuna.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥ १७ ॥
translation: Yoga killeth out all pain for him who is regulated in eating and amusement, regulated in performing actions, regulated in sleeping and waking.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते । निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥ १८ ॥
translation: When his subdued thought is fixed on the Self, free from longing after all desirable things, then it is said, "he is harmonised."

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता । योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥ १९ ॥
translation: As a lamp in a windless place flickereth not, to such is likened the Yogî of subdued thought, absorbed in the yoga of the Self.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया । यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥ २० ॥
translation: That in which the mind finds rest, quieted by the practice of yoga: that in which he, seeing the Self by the Self, in the Self is satisfied;

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद् बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् । वेत्ति यत्र न चैवाऽयं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥ २१ ॥
translation: That in which he findeth the supreme delight which the Reason can grasp beyond the senses, wherein established he moveth not from the Reality;

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः । यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणाऽपि विचाल्यते ॥ २२ ॥
translation: Which, having obtained, he thinketh there is no greater gain beyond it; wherein, established, he is not shaken even by heavy sorrow;

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.

translation: That should be known by the name of yoga, this disconnection from the union with pain. This yoga must be clung to with a firm conviction and with undesponding mind. (23

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.

translation: Abandoning without reserve all desires born of the imagination, by the mind curbing in the aggregate of the senses on every side,

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: शनैःशनैरुपरमेद्‌ बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥ २५ ॥
translation: Little by little let him gain tranquillity, by means of Reason controlled by steadiness; having made the mind abide in the Self, let him not think of anything.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥ २६ ॥
translation: As often as the wavering and unsteady mind goeth forth, so often reining it in, let him bring it under the control of the Self.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् । उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Supreme joy is for this Yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passion-nature is calmed, who is sinless and of the nature of the Eternal.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः । सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥ २८ ॥
translation: The Yogî who thus, ever harmonising the self, hath put away sin, he easily enjoyeth the infinite bliss of contact with the Eternal.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥ २९ ॥
translation: The self, harmonised by yoga, seeth the Self abiding in all beings, all beings in the Self; everywhere he seeth the same.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति । तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥ ३० ॥
translation: He who seeth Me everywhere, and seeth everything in Me, of him will I never lose hold, and he shall never lose hold of Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः । सर्वथा वर्त्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥ ३१ ॥
translation: He who, established in unity, worshippeth Me abiding in all beings, that Yogi liveth in Me, whatever his mode of living.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः ॥ ३२ ॥
translation: He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, seeth equality in everything, whether pleasant or painful, he is considered a perfect Yogî.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात्स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥ ३३ ॥
translation: This yoga which Thou hast declared to be by equanimity, O Madhusûdana, I see not a stable foundation for it, owing to restlessness;

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्‌ दृढम् । तस्याऽहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥ ३४ ॥
translation: For the mind is verily restless, O Krishna; it is impetuous, strong and difficult to bend. I deem it as hard to curb as the wind.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥ ३५ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Without doubt, O mighty-armed, the mind is hard to curb and restless; but it may be curbed by constant practice and by dispassion.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः । वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥ ३६ ॥
translation: Yoga is hard to attain, methinks, by a self that is uncontrolled; but by the Self-controlled it is attainable by properly directed energy.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥ ३७ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: He who is unsubdued but who possesseth faith, with the mind wandering away from yoga, failing to attain perfection in yoga, what path doth he tread, O Krishna?

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥ ३८ ॥
translation: Fallen from both, is he destroyed like a rent cloud, unsteadfast, O mighty-armed, deluded in the path of the Eternal?

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: एतं मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता नह्युपपद्यते ॥ ३९ ॥
translation: Deign, O Krishna, to completely dispel this doubt of mine; for there is none to be found save Thyself able to destroy this doubt.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते । न हि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद्‌दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥ ४० ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: O son of Prithâ, neither in this world nor in the life to come is there destruction for him; never doth any who worketh righteousness, O beloved, tread the path of woe.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः । शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥ ४१ ॥
translation: Having attained to the worlds of the pure-doing, and having dwelt there for immemorial years, he who fell from yoga is reborn in a pure and blessed house;

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् । एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥ ४२ ॥
translation: Or he may even be born into a family of wise Yogîs; but such a birth as that is most difficult to obtain in this world.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् । यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥ ४३ ॥
translation: There he recovereth the characteristics belonging to this former body, and with these he again laboureth for perfection, O joy of the Kurus.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥ ४४ ॥
translation: By that former practice he is irresistibly swept away. Only wishing to know yoga, even the seeker after yoga goeth beyond the Brâhmic world;

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः । अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ ४५ ॥
translation: But the Yogî, labouring with assiduity, purified from sin, fully perfected through manifold births, he reacheth the supreme goal.

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः । कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन ॥ ४६ ॥
translation: The Yogî is greater than the ascetics; he is thought to be greater than even the wise; the Yogî is greater than the men of action; therefore become thou a Yogî, O Arjuna!

chapterSummary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.
sanskrit: योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना । श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥ ४७ ॥
translation: And among all Yogîs, he who, full of faith, with the inner Self abiding in Me, adoreth Me, he is considered by Me to be the most completely harmonised.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥ १ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: With the mind clinging to me, O Pârtha, performing yoga, refuged in Me, how thou shalt without doubt know Me to the uttermost, that hear thou.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः । यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ॥ २ ॥
translation: I will declare to thee this knowledge and wisdom in its completeness, which, having known, there is nothing more here needeth to be known.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये । यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥ ३ ॥
translation: Among thousands of men scarce one striveth for perfection; of the successful strivers scarce one knoweth Me in essence.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च । अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, Mind, and Reason also and Egoism—these are the eightfold division of My nature.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् । जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत् ॥ ५ ॥
translation: This the inferior. Know My other nature, the higher, the life-element, O mighty-armed, by which the universe is upheld.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय । अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Know this to be the womb of all beings. I am the source of the forthgoing of the whole universe and likewise the place of its dissolving.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥ ७ ॥
translation: There is naught whatsoever higher than I, O Dhananjaya. All this is threaded on Me, as rows of pearls on a string.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभाऽस्मि शशिसूर्ययोः । प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥ ८ ॥
translation: I the sapidity in waters, O son of Kuntî, I the radiance in moon and sun; the Word of Power in all the Vedas, sound in ether, and virility in men;

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ । जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ॥ ९ ॥
translation: The pure fragrance of earths and the brilliance in fire am I; the life in all beings am I, and the austerity in ascetics.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् । बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥ १० ॥
translation: Know Me, O Pârtha! as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the Reason of the Reason-endowed, the splendour of splendid things am I.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: बलं बलवतामस्मि कामरागविवर्जितम् । धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥ ११ ॥
translation: And I the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and passion. In beings I am desire not contrary to duty, O Lord of the Bharatas.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये । मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥ १२ ॥
translation: The natures that are harmonious, active, slothful, these know as from Me; not I in them, but they in me.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् । मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥ १३ ॥
translation: All this world, deluded by these natures made by the three qualities, knoweth not Me, above these, imperishable.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥ १४ ॥
translation: This divine illusion of Mine, caused by the qualities, is hard to pierce; they who come to Me, they cross over this illusion.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः । माययाऽपहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥ १५॥
translation: The evil-doing, the deluded, the vilest men, they come not to Me, they whose wisdom is destroyed by illusion, who have embraced the nature of demons.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन । आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥ १६ ॥
translation: Fourfold in division are the righteous ones who worship me, O Arjuna; the suffering, the seeker for knowledge, the self-interested and the wise, O Lord of the Bhâratas.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते । प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥ १७ ॥
translation: Of these the wise, constantly harmonised, worshipping the One, is the best; I am supremely dear to the wise, and he is dear to Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् । आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥ १८ ॥
translation: Noble are all these, but I hold the wise as verily Myself; he, Self united, is fixed on Me, the highest Path.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते । वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः ॥ १९ ॥
translation: At the close of many births the man full of wisdom cometh unto Me; "Vâsudeva is all." saith he, the Mahâtmâ, very difficult to find.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः । तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥ २० ॥
translation: They whose wisdom hath been rent away by desires go forth to other Shining Ones, resorting to various external observances, according to their own natures.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयाऽर्चितुमिच्छति । तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥ २१ ॥
