translation: Any devotee who seeketh to worship with faith any such aspect, I verily bestow the unswerving faith of that man.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते । लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान्हि तान् ॥ २२ ॥
translation: He endowed with that faith, seeketh the worship of such a one, and from him he obtaineth his desires, I verily decreeing the benefits;

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् । देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥ २३ ॥
translation: Finite indeed the fruit that belongeth to those who are of small intelligence. To the Shining Ones go the worshippers of the Shining Ones, but my devotees come unto Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः । परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥ २४ ॥
translation: Those devoid of Reason think of Me, the unmanifest, as having manifestation, knowing not My supreme nature, imperishable, most excellent.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः । मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥ २५ ॥
translation: Nor am I of all discovered, enveloped in My creation-illusion. This deluded world knoweth Me not, the unborn, the imperishable.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन । भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥ २६ ॥
translation: I know the beings that are past, that are present, that are to come, O Arjuna, but no one knoweth Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत । सर्वभूतानि सम्मोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥ २७ ॥
translation: By the delusion of the pairs of opposites, sprung from attraction and repulsion, O Bhârata, all beings walk this universe wholly deluded, O Parantapa.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् । ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥ २८ ॥
translation: But those men of pure deeds, in whom sin is come to an end, they, freed from the delusive pairs of opposites, worship Me, steadfast in vows.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये । ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥ २९ ॥
translation: They who, refuged in Me, strive for liberation from birth and death, they know the Eternal, the whole Self-knowledge, and all action.

chapterSummary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.
sanskrit: साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः । प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥ ३० ॥
translation: They who know Me as the knowledge of the elements, as that of the Shining Ones, and as that of the Sacrifice, they harmonised in mind, know Me verily even in the time of forthgoing.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम । अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ॥ १ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: What is that Eternal, what Self-knowledge, what Action, O Purushottama? And what is declared to be the knowledge of the Elements, what is called the knowledge of the Shining Ones?

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन । प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ॥ २ ॥
translation: What is the knowledge of Sacrifice in this body, and how, O, Madhusûdana? And how, at the time of forthgoing art Thou known by the Self-controlled?

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते । भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः ॥ ३ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: The indestructible, the supreme is the Eternal; His essential nature is called Self-knowledge; the emanation that causes the birth of beings is named Action;

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् । अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Knowledge of the Elements concerns My perishable nature, and knowledge of the Shining Ones concerns the life-giving energy; the knowledge of Sacrifice tells of Me, as wearing the body, O best of living beings.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् । यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥ ५ ॥
translation: And he who, casting off the body, goeth forth thinking upon Me only at the time of the end, he entereth into My being: there is no doubt of that.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् । तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Whosoever at the end abandoneth the body, thinking upon any being, to that being only he goeth, O Kaunteya, ever to that conformed in nature.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥ ७ ॥
translation: Therefore at all times think upon Me only and fight. With mind and Reason set on Me, without doubt thou shalt come to Me.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना । परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥ ८ ॥
translation: With the mind not wandering after aught else, harmonised by continual practice, constantly meditating, O Pârtha, one goeth to the Spirit supreme, divine.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: कविं पुराणमनुशासितारमणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः । सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूपमादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् ॥ ९ ॥
translation: He who thinketh upon the Ancient, the Omniscient, the All-Ruler, minuter than the minute, the supporter of all, of form unimaginable, refulgent as the sun beyond the darkness,

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेन भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव । भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक् स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥ १० ॥
translation: In the time of forthgoing, with unshaken mind, fixed in devotion, by the power of yoga drawing together his life-breath in the centre of the two eyebrows, he goeth to this Spirit, supreme, divine.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः । यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति तत्ते पदं सङ्ग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये ॥ ११ ॥
translation: That which is declared indestructible by the Veda-knowers, that which the controlled and passion-free enter, that desiring which Brahmacharya is performed, that path I will declare to thee with brevity.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च । मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् ॥ १२ ॥
translation: All the gates closed, the mind confined in the heart, the life-breath fixed in his own head, concentrated by yoga,

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् । यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ १३ ॥
translation: "Aum!" the one syllabled Eternal, reciting, thinking upon Me, he who goeth forth, abandoning the body, he goeth on the highest path.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः । तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥ १४ ॥
translation: He who constantly thinketh upon Me, not thinking ever of another, of him I am easily reached, O Pârtha, of this ever-harmonised Yogî.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् । नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Having come to Me, these Mahâtmâs come not again to birth, the place of pain, non-eternal; they have gone to the highest bliss.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन । मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥ १६ ॥
translation: The worlds, beginning with the world of Brahmâ, they come and go, O Arjuna; but he who cometh unto Me, O Kaunteya, he knoweth birth no more.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः । रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥ १७ ॥
translation: The people who know the day of Brahmâ, a thousand ages in duration, and the night a thousand ages in ending, they know day and night.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे । रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके ॥ १८ ॥
translation: From the unmanifested all the manifested stream forth at the coming of day; at the coming of night they dissolve, even in That called the unmanifested.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते । रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥ १९ ॥
translation: This multitude of beings, going forth repeatedly, is dissolved at the coming of night: by ordination, O Pârtha, it streams forth at the coming of day.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः । यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥ २० ॥
translation: Therefore verily there existeth, higher than that unmanifested, another unmanifested, eternal, which in the destroying of all beings, is not destroyed. (20

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् । यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥ २१ ॥
translation: That unmanifested, "the Indestructible," It is called; It is named the highest Path. They who reach It return not. That is My supreme abode.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया । यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥ २२ ॥
translation: He, the highest Spirit, O Pârtha, may be reached by unswerving devotion to Him alone, in whom all beings abide, by whom all This is pervaded.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः । प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥ २३ ॥
translation: That time wherein going forth Yogîs return not, and also that wherein going forth they return, that time shall I declare to thee, O prince of the Bhâratas.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् । तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥ २४ ॥
translation: Fire, light, day-time, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern path—then, going forth, the men who know the Eternal go to the Eternal.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् । तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥ २५ ॥
translation: Smoke, night-time, the dark fortnight also, the six months of the southern path—then the Yogî, obtaining the moonlight, returneth.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते । एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः ॥ २६ ॥
translation: Light and darkness, these are thought to be the world's everlasting paths; by the one he goeth who returneth not, by the other he who returneth again.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन । तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Knowing these paths, O Pârtha, the Yogi is nowise perplexed. Therefore in all times be firm in yoga, O Arjuna.

chapterSummary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.
sanskrit: वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् । अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् ॥ २८ ॥
translation: The fruit of meritorious deeds, attached in the Vedas to sacrifices, to austerities, and also to almsgiving, the Yogî passeth all these by having known this, and goeth to the supreme and ancient Seat.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे । ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥ १ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: To thee, the uncarping, verily shall I declare this profoundest Secret, wisdom with knowledge combined, which, having known, thou shalt be freed from evil.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् । प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम् ॥ २ ॥
translation: Kingly Science, kingly Secret, supreme Purifier, this; intuitional, according to righteousness, very easy to perform, imperishable.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप । अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि ॥ ३ ॥
translation: Men without faith in this knowledge, O Parantapa, not reaching Me, return to the paths of this world of death.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना । मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ॥ ४ ॥
translation: By Me all this world is pervaded in My unmanifested aspect; all beings have root in Me, I am not rooted in them.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् । भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः ॥ ५ ॥
translation: Nor have beings root in Me; behold My sovereign Yoga! The support of beings, yet not rooted in beings, My Self their efficient cause.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् । तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥ ६ ॥
translation: As the mighty air everywhere moving is rooted in the Ether, so all beings rest rooted in Me—thus know thou.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् । कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् ॥ ७ ॥
translation: All beings, O Kaunteya, enter my lower nature at the end of a world-age; at the beginning of a world-age again I emanate them.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः । भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् ॥ ८ ॥
translation: Hidden in Nature, which is mine own, I emanate again and again all this multitude of beings, helpless, by the force of Nature.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय । उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु ॥ ९ ॥
translation: Nor do these works bind me, O Dhananjaya, enthroned on high unattached to actions.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: मयाऽध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् । हेतुनाऽनेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते ॥ १० ॥
translation: Under Me as supervisor, Nature sends forth the moving and unmoving: because of this, O Kaunteya, the universe revolves.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् । परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम् ॥ ११ ॥
translation: The foolish disregard Me, when clad in human semblance, ignorant of My supreme nature, the great Lord of beings;

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः । राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः ॥ १२ ॥
translation: Empty of hope, empty of deeds, empty of wisdom, senseless, partaking of the deceitful, brutal and demoniacal nature.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः । भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम् ॥ १३ ॥
translation: Verily the Mahâtmâs, O Partha, partaking of My divine nature, worship with unwavering mind, having known Me, the imperishable source of beings.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः । नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ॥ १४ ॥
translation: Always magnifying Me, strenuous, firm in vows, prostrating themselves before Me, they worship Me with devotion ever harmonised. (14

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते । एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम् ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Others also, sacrificing with the sacrifice of wisdom, worship Me as the One and the Manifold everywhere present.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम् । मन्त्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् ॥ १६ ॥
translation: I the ablation; I the sacrifice; I the ancestral offering; I the fire-giving herb; the mantram I; I also the butter; I the fire; the burnt-offering I;

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः । वेद्यं पवित्रमोङ्कार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥ १७ ॥
translation: I the Father of this universe, the Mother, the Supporter, the Grandsire, the Holy one to be known, the Word of Power, and also the Rik, Sâma, and Yajur,

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥ १८ ॥
translation: The Path, Husband, Lord, Witness, Abode, Shelter, Lover, Origin, Dissolution, Foundation, house, Seed imperishable.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च । अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन ॥ १९ ॥
translation: I give heat; I hold back and send forth the rain; immortality and also death, being and non-being am I, Arjuna.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापाः यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते । ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोकमश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् ॥ २० ॥
translation: The knowers of the three, the Soma-drinkers, the purified from sin, worshipping Me with sacrifice, pray of Me the way to heaven; they, ascending to the holy world of the Ruler of the Shining Ones, eat in heaven the divine feasts of the Shining Ones.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालम् क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति । एवं त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्नाः गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते ॥ २१ ॥
translation: They, having enjoyed the spacious heaven-world, their holiness withered, come back to this world of death. Following the virtues enjoined by the three, desiring desires, they obtain the transitory.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥ २२ ॥
translation: To those men who worship Me alone thinking of no other, to those ever harmonious, I bring full security.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: येऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः । तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् ॥ २३ ॥
translation: Even the devotees of other Shining Ones, who worship full of faith, they also worship Me, O son of Kuntî, though contrary to the ancient rule.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च । न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते ॥ २४ ॥
translation: I am indeed the enjoyer of all sacrifices and also the Lord, but they know Me not in Essence, and hence they fall.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: यान्ति देवव्रता देवान् पितॄन्यान्ति पितृव्रताः । भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् ॥ २५ ॥
translation: They who worship the Shining Ones go to the Shining Ones; to the Ancestors go the Ancestor-worshippers; to the Elements go those who sacrifice to Elementals; but My worshippers come unto Me.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥ २६ ॥
translation: He who offereth to Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, that I accept from the striving self, offered as it is with devotion.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् । यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Whatsoever thou doest, whatsoever thou eatest, whatsoever thou offerest, whatsoever thou givest, whatsoever thou doest of austerity, O Kaunteya, do thou that as an offering unto Me.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः । संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि ॥ २८ ॥
translation: Thus shalt thou be liberated from the bonds of action, yielding good and evil fruits; thyself harmonised by the yoga of renunciation, thou shalt come unto Me when set free.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः । ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥ २९ ॥
translation: The same am I to all beings; there is none hateful to Me nor dear. They verily who worship Me with devotion, they are in Me, and I also in them.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् । साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः ॥ ३० ॥
translation: Even if the most sinful worship Me, with undivided heart, he too must be accounted righteous, for he hath rightly resolved;

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति । कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥ ३१ ॥
translation: Speedily he becometh dutiful and goeth to eternal peace; O Kaunteya, know thou for certain that My devotee perisheth never.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः । स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥ ३२ ॥
translation: They who take refuge with Me, O Partha, though of the womb of sin, women, Vaishyas, even Shûdras, they also tread the highest path.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा । अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम् ॥ ३३ ॥
translation: How much rather then holy Brâhmanas and devoted royal saints; having obtained this transient joyless world, worship thou Me.

chapterTitle: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
chapterSummary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.
sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥ ३४ ॥
translation: On Me fix thy mind, be devoted to Me; sacrifice to Me; prostrate thyself before Me; harmonised thus in the Self, thou shalt come unto Me, having Me as thy supreme goal.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः । यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥ १ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Again, O mighty-armed, hear thou My supreme word, that, desiring thy welfare, I will declare to thee who art beloved.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः । अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः ॥ २ ॥
translation: The multitude of the Shining Ones, or the great Rishis, know not my forthcoming, for I am the beginning of all the Shining Ones and the great Rishis.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम् । असम्मूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
translation: He who knoweth Me, unborn, beginningless, the great Lord of the world, he among mortals without delusion, is liberated from all sin.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसम्मोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः । सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Reason, wisdom, non-illusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, pleasure, pain, existence, non-existence, fear, and also courage

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः । भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः ॥ ५ ॥
translation: Harmlessness, equanimity, content, austerity, almsgiving, fame and obloquy are the various characteristics of beings issuing from Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा । मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः ॥ ६ ॥
translation: The seven great Rishis, the ancient Four, and also the Manus, were born of My nature, and mind; of them this race was generated.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः । सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः ॥ ७ ॥
translation: He who knows in essence that sovereignty and yoga of Mine, he is harmonised by unfaltering yoga; there is no doubt thereof.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते । इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः ॥ ८ ॥
translation: I am the Generator of all; all evolves from Me; understanding thus, the wise adore Me in rapt emotion.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् । कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥ ९ ॥
translation: Mindful of Me, their life hidden in Me, illumining each other, ever conversing about Me, they are content and joyful.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् । ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते ॥ १० ॥
translation: To these, ever harmonious, worshipping in love, I give the yoga of discrimination by which they come unto Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः । नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता ॥ ११ ॥
translation: Out of pure compassion for them, dwelling within their Self, I destroy the ignorance-born darkness by the shining lamp of wisdom.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् । पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् ॥ १२ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Thou art the supreme Eternal, the supreme Abode, the supreme Purity, eternal divine man, primeval Deity, unborn, the Lord!

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा । असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे ॥ १३ ॥
translation: All the Rishis have thus acclaimed Thee, as also the divine Rishi, Nârada; so Asita, Devala, and Vyâsa; and now Thou Thyself tellest it me.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव । न हि ते भगवन्व्यक्तिं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः ॥ १४ ॥
translation: All this I believe true that Thou sayest to me, O Keshava. Thy manifestation, O Blessed Lord, neither Shining Ones nor Dânavas comprehend.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: स्वयमेवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम । भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Thyself indeed knowest Thyself by Thyself, O Purushottama; Source of beings, Lord of beings, Shining One of Shining Ones, Ruler of the world!

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः । याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि ॥ १६ ॥
translation: Deign to tell without reserve of Thine own divine glories, by which glories Thou remainest, pervading these worlds.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् । केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया ॥ १७ ॥
translation: How may I know thee, O Yogi, by constant meditation? In what, in what aspects art Thou to be thought of by me, O blessed Lord?

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन । भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि शृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् ॥ १८ ॥
translation: In detail tell me again of Thy yoga and glory, O Janardana; for me there is never satiety in hearing thy life-giving words.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः । प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे ॥ १९ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Blessed be thou! I will declare to thee My divine glory by its chief characteristics, O best of the Kurus; there is no end to details of Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः । अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥ २० ॥
translation: I, O Gudakesha, am the Self, seated in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all beings.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् । मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी ॥ २१ ॥
translation: Of the Adityas I am Vishnu; of radiances the glorious sun; I am Marîchi of the Maruts; of the asterisms the Moon am I.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः । इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥ २२ ॥
translation: Of the Vedas I am the Sâma-Veda; I am Vâsava of the Shining Ones; and of the senses I am the mind; I am of living beings the intelligence.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् । वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् ॥ २३ ॥
translation: And of the Rudras Shañkara am I; Vittesha of the Yakshas and Râkshasas; and of the Vasus I am Pâvaka; Meru of high mountains am I.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् । सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥ २४ ॥
translation: And know Me, O Pârtha, of household priests the chief, Brihaspati: of generals I am Skanda; of lakes I am the ocean.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् । यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः ॥ २५ ॥
translation: Of the great Rishis Bhṛigu; of speech I am the one syllable; of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetitions; of immovable things the Himâlaya.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः । गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः ॥ २६ ॥
translation: Asvattha of all tree; and of divine Rishis Nârada; of Gandharvas Chitraratha; of the perfected the Muni Kapila.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् । ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Uchchaishravas of horses know me, nectar-born; Airâvata of lordly elephants, and of men the Monarch.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् । प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः ॥ २८ ॥
translation: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt; of cows I am Kâmadhuk; I am Kandarpa of the progenitors; of serpents Vâsuki am I.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् । पितॄणामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् ॥ २९ ॥
translation: And I am Ananta of Nâgas, Varuna of sea-dwellers I; and of ancestors Aryaman; Yama of governors am I.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् । मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् ॥ ३० ॥
translation: And I am Prahlâda of Daityas; of calculators Time am I; and of wild beasts I the imperial beast; and Vainateya of birds.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् । झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी ॥ ३१ ॥
translation: Of purifiers I am the wind; Rama of warriors I; and I am Makara of fishes; of streams the Gangâ am I.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन । अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् ॥ ३२ ॥
translation: Of creations the beginning and the ending, and also the middle am I, O Arjuna. Of sciences the science concerning the Self; the speech of orators I.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च । अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः ॥ ३३ ॥
translation: Of letters the letter A I am, and the duality of a compound; I also everlasting Time; I the Supporter, whose face turns everywhere.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् । कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥ ३४ ॥
translation: And all-devouring Death am I, and the origin of all to come; and of feminine qualities, fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, constancy, forgiveness.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् । मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः ॥ ३५ ॥
translation: Of hymns also Brihatsâman; Gâyatrî of metres am I; of months I am Mârgasîrsha; of seasons the flowery.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् । जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् ॥ ३६ ॥
translation: I am the gambling of the cheat, and the splendour of splendid things I; I am victory, I am determination, and the truth of the truthful I.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनञ्जयः । मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः ॥ ३७ ॥
translation: Of the Vṛishnis Vâsudeva am I; of the Pândavas Dhananjaya; of the Sages also I am Vyâsa; of poets Ushanâ the Bard.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् । मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् ॥ ३८ ॥
translation: Of rulers I am the sceptre; of those that seek victory I am statesmanship; and of secrets I am also silence; the knowledge of knowers am I.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन । न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् ॥ ३९ ॥
translation: And whatsoever is the seed of all beings, that am I, O Arjuna; nor is there aught, moving or unmoving, that may exist bereft of Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परन्तप । एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया ॥ ४० ॥
translation: There is no end of My divine powers, O Parantapa. What has been declared is illustrative of My infinite glory.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसम्भवम् ॥ ४१ ॥
translation: Whatsoever is glorious, good, beautiful, and mighty, understand thou that to go forth from a fragment of My splendour.

chapterSummary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.
sanskrit: अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन । विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत् ॥ ४२ ॥
translation: But what is the knowledge of all these details to thee, O Arjuna? Having pervaded this whole universe with one fragment of Myself, I remain.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् । यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम ॥ १ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: This word of the supreme Secret concerning the Self, Thou hast spoken out of compassion; by this my delusion is taken away.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया । त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् ॥ २ ॥
translation: The production and destruction of beings have been heard by me in detail from Thee, O Lotus-eyed, and also Thy imperishable greatness.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: एवमेतद्यथाऽऽत्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर । द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम ॥ ३ ॥
translation: O supreme Lord, even as Thou describest Thyself, O best of beings, I desire to see Thy Form omnipotent.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो । योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयात्मानमव्ययम् ॥ ४ ॥
translation: If Thou thinkest that by me It can be seen, O Lord, Lord of Yoga, then show me Thine imperishable Self.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः । नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च ॥ ५ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Behold, O Pârtha, a Form of Me, a hundredfold, a thousandfold, various in kind, divine, various in colours and shapes.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्विनौ मरुतस्तथा । बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याश्चर्याणि भारत ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Behold the Âdityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins and also the Maruts; behold many marvels never seen ere this, O Bhârata.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् । मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि ॥ ७ ॥
translation: Here, to-day, behold the whole universe, movable and immovable, standing in one in My body, O Gudâkesha, with aught else thou desirest to see.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा । दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ॥ ८ ॥
translation: But verily thou art not able to behold Me with these thine eyes; the divine eye I give unto thee. Behold My sovereign Yoga.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन् महायोगेश्वरो हरिः । दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम् ॥ ९ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: Having thus spoken, O King, the great Lord of Yoga, Hari, showed to Pârtha His supreme Form as Lord.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् । अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम् ॥ १० ॥
translation: With many mouths and eyes, with many visions of marvel, with many divine ornaments, with many upraised divine weapons;

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम् । सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम् ॥ ११ ॥
translation: Wearing divine necklaces and vestures, anointed with divine unguents, the God all-marvellous, boundless, with face turned everywhere.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता । यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥ १२ ॥
translation: If the splendour of a thousand suns were to blaze out together in the sky, that might resemble the glory of that Mahâtman.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा । अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा ॥ १३ ॥
translation: There Pândava beheld the whole universe, divided into manifold parts, standing in one in the body of the Deity of Deities.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः । प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत ॥ १४ ॥
translation: Then he, Dhananjaya, overwhelmed with astonishment, his hair upstanding, bowed down his head to the Shining One, and with joined palms spake.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान् । ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थमृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Within Thy Form, O God, the Gods I see, All grades of beings with distinctive marks; Brahma, the Lord, upon His lotus-throne, The Rishis all, and Serpents, the Divine.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रम् पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् । नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिम् पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥ १६ ॥
translation: With mouths, eyes, arms, breasts multitudinous, I see Thee everywhere, unbounded Form. Beginning, middle, end, nor source of Thee, Infinite Lord, infinite Form, I find;

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च तेजोराशिं सर्वतो दीप्तिमन्तम् । पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ताद् दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् ॥ १७ ॥
translation: Shining, a mass of splendour everywhere, With discus, mace, tiara, I behold: Blazing as fire, as sun dazzling the gaze, From all sides in the sky, immeasurable.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यम् त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् । त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे ॥ १८ ॥
translation: Lofty beyond all thought, unperishing, Thou treasure-house supreme, all-immanent; Eternal Dharma's changeless Guardian, Thou; As immemorial Man I think of Thee.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य- मनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम् । पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम् स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम् ॥ १९ ॥
translation: Nor source, nor midst, nor end; infinite force, Unnumbered arms, the sun and moon Thine eyes  I see Thy face, as sacrificial fire Blazing, its splendour burneth up the worlds.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः । दृष्ट्वाऽद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदम् लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् ॥ २० ॥
translation: By Thee alone are filled the earth, the heavens, And all the regions that are stretched between; The triple worlds sink down, O mighty One, Before Thine awful manifested Form.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घा विशन्ति केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति । स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः ॥ २१ ॥
translation: To Thee the troops of Suras enter in, Some with joined palms in awe invoking Thee; Banded Maharshis, Siddhas, cry: "All hail"! Chanting Thy praises with resounding songs.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्याः विश्वेऽश्विनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च । गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घाः वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे ॥ २२ ॥
translation: Rudras, Vasus, Sâdhyas and Adityas, Vishvas, the Ashvins, Maruts, Ushmapas, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Siddhas, Asuras, In wondering multitudes beholding Thee.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रम् महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम् । बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालम् दृष्ट्वा लोका प्रव्यथितास्तथाऽहम् ॥ २३ ॥
translation: Thy mighty Form, with many mouths and eyes, Long armed, with thighs and feet innumerate, Vast-bosomed, set with many fearful teeth, The worlds see terror-struck, as also I.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: नभः स्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णम् व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् । दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥ २४ ॥
translation: Radiant, Thou touchest heaven, rainbow-hued, With opened mouths and shining vast-orbed eyes. My inmost self is quaking, having seen, My strength is withered, Vishnu, and my peace.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि । दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥ २५ ॥
translation: Like Time's destroying flames I see Thy teeth, Upstanding, spread within expanded jaws; Nought know I anywhere, no shelter find; Mercy, O God! re of all the worlds!

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः सर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः । भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथाऽसौ सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः ॥ २६ ॥
translation: The sons of Dhṛitarâshtra, and with them The multitude of all these kings of earth, Bhîshma, and Drona, Sûta's royal son, And all the noblest warriors of our hosts,

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्ति दंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि । केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु संदृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Into Thy gaping mouths they hurrying rush, Tremendous-toothed and terrible to see; Some caught within the gaps between Thy teeth Are seen, their heads to powder crushed and ground.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाः समुद्रमेवाभिमुखा द्रवन्ति । तथा तवामी नरलोकवीराः विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति ॥ २८ ॥
translation: As river-floods impetuously rush, Hurling their waters into ocean's lap, So fling themselves into Thy flaming mouths, In haste, these mighty men, these lords of earth.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गाः विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः । तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोका- स्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः ॥ २९ ॥
translation: As moths with quickened speed will headlong fly Into a flaming light, to fall destroyed, So also these, in haste precipitate, Enter within Thy mouths destroyed to fall.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ता- ल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः । तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रम् भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो ॥ ३० ॥
translation: On every side, all-swallowing, fiery-tongued, Thou lickest up mankind, devouring all; The glory filleth space: the universe Is burning, Vishnu, with Thy blazing rays.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद । विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यम् न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम् ॥ ३१ ॥
translation: Reveal Thy Self; what awful Form art Thou? I worship Thee! Have mercy, God supreme! Thine inner Being I am fain to know; This Thy forth-streaming Life bewilders me.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः । ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः ॥ ३२ ॥
translation: Time am I, laying desolate the world, Made manifest on earth to slay mankind! Not one of all these warriors ranged for strife Escapeth death; thou shalt alone survive.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व जित्वा शत्रून्भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् । मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् ॥ ३३ ॥
translation: Therefore stand up! win for thyself renown, Conquer thy foes, enjoy the wealth filled realm, By Me they are already overcome, Be thou the outward cause, left-handed one.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च कर्णं तथाऽन्यानपि योधवीरान् । मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठाः युद्ध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान् ॥ ३४ ॥
translation: Drona and Bhîshma and Jayadratha, Karna, and all the other warriors here, Are slain by Me. Destroy them fearlessly. Fight! thou shalt crush thy rivals in the field.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी । नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णम् सगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य ॥ ३५ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: Having heard these words of Keshava, he who weareth a diadem, with joined palms, quaking and prostrating himself, spake again to Krishna, stammering with fear, casting down his face.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च । रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः ॥ ३६ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Hrishîkesha! in Thy magnificence Rightly the world rejoiceth, hymning Thee; The Râkshasas to every quarter fly In fear; the hosts of Siddhas prostrate fall.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन् गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे । अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास त्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत् ॥ ३७ ॥
translation: How should they otherwise, O loftiest Self! First Cause! Brahmâ Himself less great than Thou. Infinite, God of Gods, home of all worlds, Unperishing, Sat, Asat, That supreme!

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
