chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराणस्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् । वेत्ताऽसि वेद्यं च परं च धाम त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप ॥ ३८ ॥
translation: First of the Gods, most ancient Man Thou art. Supreme receptacle of all that lives; Knower and known, the dwelling-place on high; In Thy vast Form the universe is spread.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च । नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते ॥ ३९ ॥
translation: Thou art Vâyu and Yama, Agni, moon, Varuna, Father, Grandsire of all; Hail, hail to Thee! a thousand times all hail! Hail unto Thee! again, again all hail!

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व । अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वम् सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः ॥ ४० ॥
translation: Prostrate in front of Thee, prostrate behind; Prostrate on every side to Thee, O All. In power boundless, measureless in strength, Thou holdest all: then Thou Thyself art All.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तम् हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति । अजानता महिमानं तवेदम् मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥ ४१ ॥
translation: If, thinking Thee but friend, importunate, O Krishna! or O Yâdava! O friend! I cried, unknowing of Thy majesty, And careless in the fondness of my love;

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु । एकोऽथवाऽप्यच्युत तत्समक्षम् तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥ ४२ ॥
translation: If jesting I irreverence showed to Thee, At play, reposing, sitting or at meals, Alone, O sinless One, or with my friends, Forgive my error, O Thou boundless One.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: पिताऽसि लोकस्य चराचरस्य त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् । न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभावः ॥ ४३ ॥
translation: Father of worlds, of all that moves and stands, Worthier of reverence than the Guru's self,  There is none like to Thee. Who passeth Thee? Pre-eminent Thy power in all the worlds.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायम् प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् । पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥ ४४ ॥
translation: Therefore I fall before Thee; with my body I worship as it fitting; bless Thou me. As father with the son, as friend with friend, With the beloved as lover, bear with me.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे । तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपम् प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥ ४५ ॥
translation: I have seen that which none hath seen before, My heart is glad, yet faileth me for fear; Show me, O God, Thine other Form again— Mercy, O God of Gods, home of all worlds—

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्तमिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव । तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते ॥ ४६ ॥
translation: Diademed, mace and discus in Thy hand. Again I fain would see Thee as before; Put on again Thy four-armed shape, O Lord, O thousand-armed, of forms innumerate.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदम् रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् । तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यम् यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् ॥ ४७ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Arjuna, by My favour thou hast seen, This loftiest Form by yoga's self revealed!  Radiant, all-penetrating, endless, first, That none except thyself hath ever seen.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानैर्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः । एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर ॥ ४८ ॥
translation: Nor sacrifice, nor Vedas, alms, nor works, Nor sharp austerity, nor study deep, Can win the vision of this Form for man, Foremost of Kurus, thou alone hast seen.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् । व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वम् तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥ ४९ ॥
translation: Be not bewildered, be thou not afraid, Because thou hast beheld this awful Form; Cast fear away, and let thy heart rejoice; Behold again Mine own familiar shape.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः । आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनम् भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥ ५० ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: Vâsudeva, having thus spoken to Arjuna, again manifested His own Form, and consoled the terrified one, the Mahâtman again assuming a gentle form.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्दन । इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥ ५१ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Beholding again Thy gentle human Form, O Janârdana, I am now collected, and am restored to my own nature.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम । देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः ॥ ५२ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: This Form of Mine beholden by thee is very hard to see. Verily the Shining Ones ever long to behold this form.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया । शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा ॥ ५३ ॥
translation: Nor can I be seen as thou hast seen Me by the Vedas, nor by austerities, nor by alms, or by offerings;

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्य अहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन । ज्ञातुं द्रष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परन्तप ॥ ५४ ॥
translation: But by devotion to Me alone I may thus be perceived, Arjuna, and known and seen in essence, and entered, O Parantapa.

chapterTitle: The Vision of the Universal Form
chapterSummary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.
sanskrit: मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः । निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥ ५५ ॥
translation: He who doeth actions for Me, whose supreme good I am, My devotee, freed from attachment without hatred of any being, he cometh unto Me, O Pândava.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते । ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥ १ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Those devotees who ever harmonised worship Thee, and those also who worship the Indestructible, the Unmanifested, whether of these is the more learned in yoga?

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते । श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥ २ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: They who with mind fixed on Me ever harmonised worship Me, with faith supreme endowed, these, in My opinion, are best in yoga.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते । सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् ॥ ३ ॥
translation: They who worship the Indestructible, the Ineffable, the unmanifested, Omnipresent, and Unthinkable, the Unchanging, Immutable, Eternal,

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः । ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Restraining and subduing the senses, regarding everything equally, in the welfare of all rejoicing, these also come unto Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् । अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते ॥ ५ ॥
translation: The difficulty of those whose minds are set on the Unmanifested is greater; for the path of the Unmanifested is hard for the embodied to reach.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Those verily who, renouncing all actions in Me and intent on Me, worship meditating on Me, with whole-hearted yoga,

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि न चिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥ ७ ॥
translation: These I speedily lift up from the ocean of death and existence, O Pârtha, their minds being fixed on Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय । निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥ ८ ॥
translation: Place thy mind in me, into Me let thy Reason enter; then without doubt thou shalt abide in Me hereafter.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् । अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥ ९ ॥
translation: And if thou art not able firmly to fix thy mind on Me, then by the yoga of practice seek to reach Me, O Dhananjaya.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव । मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन्सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥ १० ॥
translation: If also thou art not equal to constant practice, be intent on My service; performing actions for My sake, thou shalt attain perfection.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥ ११ ॥
translation: If even to do this thou hast not strength, then, taking refuge in union with Me, renounce all fruit of action with the self controlled.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते । ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् ॥ १२ ॥
translation: Better indeed is wisdom than constant-practice; than wisdom, meditation is better; than meditation, renunciation of the fruit of action; on renunciation follows peace.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥ १३ ॥
translation: He who beareth no ill-will to any being, friendly and compassionate, without attachment and egoism, balanced in pleasure and pain, and forgiving,

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मे भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥ १४ ॥
translation: Ever content, harmonious, with the self-controlled, resolute, with mind and Reason dedicated to Me, he, My devotee, is dear to Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः । हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥ १५ ॥
translation: He from whom the world doth not shrink away, who doth not shrink away from the world, freed from the anxieties of joy, anger, and fear, he is dear to me.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥ १६ ॥
translation: He who wants nothing, is pure, expert, passionless, untroubled, renouncing every undertaking, he, My devotee, is dear to Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥ १७ ॥
translation: He who neither loveth nor hateth, nor grieveth, nor desireth, renouncing good and evil, full of devotion, he is dear to Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानपमानयोः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥ १८ ॥
translation: Alike to foe and friend, and also in fame and ignominy, alike in cold and heat, pleasures and pains, destitute of attachment,

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् । अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥ १९ ॥
translation: Taking equally praise and reproach, silent, wholly content with what cometh, homeless, firm in mind, full of devotion, that man is dear to Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.
sanskrit: ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते । श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः ॥ २० ॥
translation: They verily who partake of this life-giving wisdom as taught herein, endued with faith, I their supreme Object, devotees, they are surpassingly dear to Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च । एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव ॥ १ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Matter and Spirit, even the Field and the Knower of the Field, wisdom and that which ought to be known, these I fain would learn, O Keshava.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । इदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते । एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥ २ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: This body, son of Kuntî, is called the Field; that which knoweth it is called the Knower of the Field by the Sages.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत । क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम ॥ ३ ॥
translation: Understand Me as the Knower of the Field in all Fields, O Bhârata. Wisdom as to the Field and the Knower of the Field, that in My opinion is the wisdom.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् । स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु ॥ ४ ॥
translation: What that Field is and of what nature, how modified, and whence it is, and what He is and what His powers, hear that now briefly from Me.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् । ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्चितैः ॥ ५ ॥
translation: Rishis have sung in manifold ways, in many various chants, and in decisive Brahma-sûtra verses full of reasonings.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च । इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः ॥ ६ ॥
translation: The great Elements, Individuality, Reason, and also the unmanifested, the ten senses and the one, and the five pastures of the senses;

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतना धृतिः । एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् ॥ ७ ॥
translation: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, combination, intelligence, firmness; these, briefly described, constitute the Field and its modifications.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् । आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः ॥ ८ ॥
translation: Humility, unpretentiousness, harmlessness, forgiveness, rectitude, service of the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-control.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च । जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् ॥ ९ ॥
translation: Dispassion towards the objects of the senses, and also absence of egoism, insight into the pain and evil of birth, death, old age and sickness,

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु । नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु ॥ १० ॥
translation: Unattachment, absence of self-identification with son, wife or home, and constant balance of mind in wished-for and unwished-for events,

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी । विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि ॥ ११ ॥
translation: Unflinching devotion to Me by yoga, without other objects, resort to sequestered places, absence of enjoyment in the company of men,

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम् । एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा ॥ १२ ॥
translation: Constancy in the wisdom of the Self, understanding of the object of essential wisdom; that is declared to be the Wisdom; all against it is ignorance.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते । अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते ॥ १३ ॥
translation: I will declare that which ought to be known, that which being known immortality is enjoyed—the beginningless supreme Eternal, called neither being nor non-being.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् । सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥ १४ ॥
translation: Everywhere That hath hands and feet, everywhere eyes, heads, and mouths; all-hearing, He dwelleth in the world, enveloping all,

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् । असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Shining with all sense-faculties without any senses; unattached supporting everything and free from qualities enjoying qualities;

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च । सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् ॥ १६ ॥
translation: Without and within all beings, immovable and also movable; by reason of His subtlety imperceptible; at hand and far away is That.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् । भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥ १७ ॥
translation: Not divided amid beings, and yet seated distributively; that is to be known as the supporter of beings; He devours and He generates.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते । ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य धिष्ठितम् ॥ १८ ॥
translation: That, the Light of all lights, is said to be beyond darkness; Wisdom, the Object of Wisdom, by Wisdom to be reached, seated in the hearts of all.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः । मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते ॥ १९ ॥
translation: Thus the Field, Wisdom and the Object of Wisdom, have been briefly told. My devotee, thus knowing, enters into My Being.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि । विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान् ॥ २० ॥
translation: Know thou that Matter and Spirit are both without beginning; and know thou also that modifications and qualities are all Matter-born.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते । पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते ॥ २१ ॥
translation: Matter is called the cause of the generation of causes and effects; Spirit is called the cause of the enjoyment of pleasure and pain.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्‌क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् । कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥ २२ ॥
translation: Spirit seated in Matter useth the qualities born of Matter; attachment to the qualities is the cause of his births in good and evil wombs.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः । परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः ॥ २३ ॥
translation: Supervisor and permitter, supporter, enjoyer, the great Lord, and also the supreme Self; thus is styled in this body the supreme Spirit.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह । सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥ २४ ॥
translation: He who thus knoweth Spirit and Matter with its qualities, in whatsoever condition he may be, he shall not be born again.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना । अन्ये साङ्ख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥ २५ ॥
translation: Some by meditation behold the Self in the self by the Self; others by the Sânkhya Yoga, and others by the Yoga of Action;

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते । तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥ २६ ॥
translation: Others also, ignorant of this, having heard of it from others, worship; and these also cross beyond death, adhering to what they had heard.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् । क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Whatsoever creature is born immobile or mobile, know thou, O best of the Bhâratas, that it is from the union between the Field and the Knower of the Field.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् । विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥ २८ ॥
translation: Seated equally in all beings, the supreme Lord, unperishing within the perishing—he who thus seeth, he seeth.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् । न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ २९ ॥
translation: Seeing indeed everywhere the same Lord equally dwelling, he doth not destroy the Self, and thus treads the highest Path.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः । यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति ॥ ३० ॥
translation: He who seeth that Matter verily performeth all actions, and that the Self is actionless, he seeth.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति । तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥ ३१ ॥
translation: When he perceiveth the diversified existence of beings as rooted in One, and spreading forth from it, then he reacheth the Eternal

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्माऽयमव्ययः । शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥ ३२ ॥
translation: Being beginningless and without qualities, the imperishable supreme Self, though seated in the body, O Kaunteya, worketh not nor is affected.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽमा नोपलिप्यते ॥ ३३ ॥
translation: As the omnipresent ether is not affected, by reason of its subtlety, so seated everywhere in the body the Self is not affected.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः । क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥ ३४ ॥
translation: As the one sun illumineth the whole earth, so the Lord of the Field illumineth the whole Field, O Bhârata.

chapterSummary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.
sanskrit: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा । भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥ ३५ ॥
translation: They who by the eyes of Wisdom perceive this difference between the Field and the Knower of the Field, and the liberation of beings from Matter they go to the Supreme.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् । यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥ १ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: I will again proclaim that supreme Wisdom, of all wisdom the best, which having known, all the Sages have gone hence to the supreme Perfection.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः । सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥ २ ॥
translation: Having taken refuge in this Wisdom and being assimilated to My own nature, they are not re-born even in the emanation of a universe, nor are disquieted in the dissolution.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम् । सम्भवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत ॥ ३ ॥
translation: My womb is the great Eternal; in that I place the germ; thence cometh the birth of all beings, O Bhârata.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः संभवन्ति याः । तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥ ४ ॥
translation: In whatsoever wombs mortals are produced, O Kaunteya, the great Eternal is their womb, I their generating father.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः । निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥ ५ ॥
translation: Harmony, Motion, Inertia, such are the qualities, Matter-born; they bind fast in the body, O great-armed one, the indestructible dweller in the body.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् । सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Of these Harmony from its stainlessness, luminous and healthy, bindeth by the attachment to bliss and the attachment to wisdom, O sinless one.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् । तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥ ७ ॥
translation: Motion, the passion nature, know thou, is the source of attachment and thirst for life, O Kaunteya, that bindeth the dweller in the body by the attachment to action.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् । प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥ ८ ॥
translation: But Inertia, know thou, born of unwisdom, is the deluder of all dwellers in the body; that bindeth by heedlessness, indolence and sloth, O Bharata.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत । ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत ॥ ९ ॥
translation: Harmony attacheth to bliss, Motion to action O Bharata. Inertia, verily, having shrouded wisdom, attacheth on the contrary to heedlessness.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत । रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥ १० ॥
translation: Now Harmony prevaileth, having overpowered Motion and Inertia, O Bhârata; now Motion, having overpowered Harmony and Inertia; and now Inertia, having overpowered Harmony and Motion.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते । ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत ॥ ११ ॥
translation: When the wisdom-light streameth forth from all the gates of the body, then it may be known that Harmony is increasing.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारंभः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥ १२ ॥
translation: Greed, outgoing energy, undertaking of actions, restlessness, desire—these are born of the increase of Motion, O best of the Bhâratas.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च । तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥ १३ ॥
translation: Darkness, stagnation and heedlessness and also delusion—these are born of the increase of Inertia, O joy of the Kurus.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् । तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥ १४ ॥
translation: If Harmony verily prevaileth when the embodied goeth to dissolution, then he goeth forth to the spotless worlds of the great Sages.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते । तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Having gone to dissolution in Motion, he is born among those attached to action; if dissolved in Inertia, he is born in the wombs of the senseless.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् । रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् ॥ १६ ॥
translation: It is said the fruit of a good action is harmonious and spotless; verily the fruit of Motion is pain, and the fruit of Inertia unwisdom

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च । प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ॥ १७ ॥
translation: From Harmony wisdom is born, and also greed from Motion; heedlessness and delusion are of Inertia and also unwisdom.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः । जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः ॥ १८ ॥
translation: They rise upwards who are settled in Harmony; the Active dwell in the mid-most place: the Inert go downwards, enveloped in the vilest

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टाऽनुपश्यति । गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥ १९ ॥
translation: When the Seer perceiveth no agent other than the qualities, and knoweth That which is higher than the qualities, he entereth into My Nature.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् । जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते ॥ २० ॥
translation: When the dweller in the body hath crossed over these three qualities, whence all bodies have been produced, liberated from birth, death, old age and sorrow, he drinketh the nectar of immortality.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । कैर्लिङ्गैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो । किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते ॥ २१ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: What are the marks of him who hath crossed over the three qualities, O Lord? How acteth he, and how doth he go beyond these three qualities?

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव । न द्वेष्टि संप्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥ २२ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: He, O Pândava, who hateth not radiance, nor outgoing energy, nor even delusion, when present, nor longeth after them, absent;

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते । गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥ २३ ॥
translation: He who, seated as a neutral, is unshaken by the qualities; who, saying, "The qualities revolve," standeth apart immovable.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः । तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः ॥ २४ ॥
translation: Balanced in pleasure and pain, self-reliant, to whom a lump of earth, a rock and gold are alike, the same to loved and unloved, firm, the same in censure and in praise,

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः । सर्वारंभपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥ २५ ॥
translation: The same in honour and ignominy, the same to friend and foe, abandoning all undertakings—he is said to have crossed over the qualities.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते । स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥ २६ ॥
translation: And he who serveth Me exclusively by the Yoga of devotion, he, crossing beyond the qualities, he is fit to become the Eternal.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.
sanskrit: ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च । शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च ॥ २७ ॥
translation: For I am the abode of the Eternal, and of the indestructible nectar of immortality, of immemorial righteousness, and of unending bliss.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् । छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥ १ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: With roots above, branches below, the Asvattha is said to be indestructible; the leaves of it are hymns; he who knoweth it is a Veda-knower.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखाः गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः । अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥ २ ॥
translation: Downwards and upwards spread the branches of it, nourished by the qualities; the objects of the senses its buds; and its roots grow downwards, the bonds of action in the world of men.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा । अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूलमसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥ ३ ॥
translation: Nor here may be acquired knowledge of its form, nor its end, nor its origin, nor its rooting-place; this strongly rooted Asvattha having been cut down by the unswerving weapon of non-attachment,

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यम् यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः । तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ॥ ४ ॥
translation: That path beyond may be sought, treading which there is no return. I go indeed to that Primal Man, whence the ancient energy forth-streamed.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषाः अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः । द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै- र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥ ५ ॥
translation: Without pride and delusion, victorious over the vice of attachment, dwelling constantly in the Self, desire pacified, liberated from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, they tread, undeluded, that indestructible path.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः । यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Nor doth the sun lighten there, nor moon, nor fire; having gone thither they return not; that is My supreme abode.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः । मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥ ७ ॥
translation: A portion of Mine own Self, transformed in the world of life into an immortal Spirit, draweth round itself the senses of which the mind is the sixth, veiled in matter.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः । गृहित्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥ ८ ॥
translation: When the Lord acquireth a body and when He abandoneth it, He seizeth these and goeth with them, as the wind takes fragrances from their retreats

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च । अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते ॥ ९ ॥
translation: Enshrined in the ear, the eye, the touch, the taste and the smell, and in the mind also, He enjoyeth the objects of the senses

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् । विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥ १० ॥
translation: The deluded do not perceive (Him) when He departeth or stayeth or enjoyeth, swayed by the qualities; the wisdom-eyed perceive.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् । यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥ ११ ॥
translation: Yogîs also, struggling, perceive Him, established in the Self; but though struggling, the unintelligent perceive Him not, their selves untrained.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् । यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् ॥ १२ ॥
translation: That splendour issuing from the sun that enlighteneth the whole world, that which is in the moon and in fire, that splendour know as from Me.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा । पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥ १३ ॥
translation: Permeating the soil, I support beings by my vital energy, and having become the delicious Soma I nourish all plants.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः । प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् ॥ १४ ॥
translation: I, having become the Fire of Life, take possession of the bodies of breathing things, and united with the life-breaths, I digest the four kinds of food.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च । वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥ १५ ॥
translation: And I am seated in the hearts of all, and from Me memory and wisdom and their absence. And that which is to be known in all the Vedas am I; and I indeed the Veda-knower and the author of the Vedanta.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च । क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥ १६ ॥
translation: There are two Energies in this world, the destructible and the indestructible; the destructible is all beings, the unchanging is called the indestructible.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः । यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥ १७ ॥
translation: The highest Energy is verily Another, declared as the Supreme Self, He who, pervading all, sustaineth the three worlds, the indestructible Lord.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः । अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ १८ ॥
translation: Since I excel the destructible, and am more excellent also than the indestructible, in the world and in the Veda I am proclaimed the Supreme Spirit.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: यो मामेवमसंमूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् । स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत ॥ १९ ॥
translation: He who undeluded knoweth Me thus as the Supreme Spirit, he, all-knowing, worshippeth Me with his whole being, O Bhârata.

chapterSummary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.
sanskrit: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ । एतद्‌बुध्वा बुद्धिमान् स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥ २० ॥
translation: Thus by Me this most secret teaching hath been told O sinless one. This known, he hath become illuminated and hath finished his work, O Bhârata.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः । दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥ १ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, cleanness of life, steadfastness in the Yoga of wisdom, almsgiving, self-restraint and sacrifice and study of the Scriptures, austerity and straightforwardness,

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् । दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥ २ ॥
translation: Harmlessness, truth, absence of wrath, renunciation, peacefulness, absence of crookedness, compassion to living beings, uncovetousness, mildness, modesty, absence of fickleness,

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता । भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥ ३ ॥
translation: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of envy and pride—these are his who is born with the divine properties, O Bhârata.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च । अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Hypocrisy, arrogance and conceit, wrath and also harshness and unwisdom are his who is born, O Pârtha, with demoniacal properties.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता । मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥ ५ ॥
translation: The divine properties are deemed to be for liberation, the demoniacal for bondage. Grieve not, thou art born with divine properties, O Pândava.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च । दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Twofold is the animal creation in this world, the divine and the demoniacal: the divine hath been described at length: hear from Me, O Pârtha, the demoniacal.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः । न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥ ७ ॥
translation: Demoniacal men know neither right energy nor right abstinence; nor purity, nor even propriety, nor truth is in them.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् । अपरस्परसंभूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम् ॥ ८ ॥
translation: "The universe is without truth, without basis," they say, "without a God; brought about by mutual union, and caused by lust and nothing else."

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: एतव दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः । प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥ ९ ॥
translation: Holding this view, these ruined selves of small understanding, of fierce deeds, come forth as enemies for the destruction of the world.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः । मोहाद्‌गृहीत्वाऽसद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः ॥ १० ॥
translation: Surrendering themselves to insatiable desires, possessed with vanity, conceit and arrogance, holding evil ideas through delusion, they engage in action with impure resolves.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः । कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः ॥ ११ ॥
translation: Giving themselves over to unmeasured thought whose end is death, regarding the gratification of desires as the highest, feeling sure that this is all,

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः । ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् ॥ १२ ॥
translation: Held in bondage by a hundred ties of expectation, given over to lust and anger, they strive to obtain by unlawful means hoards of wealth for sensual enjoyments.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् । इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥ १३ ॥
translation: "This to-day by me hath been won, that purpose I shall gain; this wealth is mine already, and also this shall be mine in future.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि । ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी ॥ १४ ॥
translation: "I have slain this enemy, and others also I shall slay. I am the Lord, I am the enjoyer, I am perfect, powerful, happy;

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया । यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥ १५ ॥
translation: "I am wealthy, well-born; what other is there that is like unto me? I will sacrifice, I will give alms, I will rejoice." Thus deluded by unwisdom,

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः । प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥ १६ ॥
translation: Bewildered by numerous thoughts, enmeshed in the web of delusion, addicted to the gratification of desire, they fall downwards into a foul hell.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: आत्मसंभाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः । यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥ १७ ॥
translation: Self-glorifying, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform lip-sacrifices for ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinance.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः । मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः ॥ १८ ॥
translation: Given over to egoism, power, insolence, lust and wrath, these malicious ones hate Me in the bodies of others and in their own.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् । क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥ १९ ॥
translation: These haters, evil, pitiless, vilest among men in the world, I ever throw down into demoniacal wombs.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि । मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥ २० ॥
translation: Cast into demoniacal wombs, deluded birth after birth, attaining not to Me, O Kaunteya, they sink into the lowest depths.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः । कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥ २१ ॥
translation: Triple is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self—lust, wrath, and greed; therefore let man renounce these three.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः । आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ २२ ॥
translation: A man liberated from these three gates of darkness, O son of Kunti, accomplisheth his own welfare, and thus reacheth the highest goal.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः । न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥ २३ ॥
translation: He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the Scriptures, followeth the promptings of desire, attaineth not to perfection, nor happiness, nor the highest goal.

chapterTitle: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
chapterSummary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.
sanskrit: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ । ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि ॥ २४ ॥
translation: Therefore let the Scriptures be thy authority, in determining what ought to be done, or what ought not to be done. Knowing what hath been declared by the ordinances of the Scriptures, thou oughtest to work in this world.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः । तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥ १ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Those that sacrifice full of faith, but casting aside the ordinances of the Scriptures, what is verily their condition, O Krishna? Is it one of Purity, Passion, or Darkness?

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा । सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु ॥ २ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Threefold is by nature the inborn faith of the embodied—pure, passionate, and dark. Hear thou of these.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत । श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥ ३ ॥
translation: The faith of each is shaped to his own nature, O Bhârata. The man consists of his faith; that which his faith is, he is even that.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः । प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Pure men worship the Gods; the passionate the gnomes and giants; the others, the dark folk, worship ghosts and troops of nature-spirits.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः । दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः ॥ ५ ॥
translation: The men who perform severe austerities, unenjoined by the Scriptures, wedded to vanity and egoism, impelled by the force of their desires and passions,

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: कर्शयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः । मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥ ६ ॥
translation: Unintelligent, tormenting the aggregated elements forming the body, and Me also, seated in the inner body, know these demoniacal in their resolves.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः । यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु ॥ ७ ॥
translation: The food also which is dear to each is threefold, as also sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Hear thou the distinction of these.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः । रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥ ८ ॥
translation: The foods that augment vitality, energy, vigour, health, joy and cheerfulness, delicious, bland, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the pure.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: कट्‌वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः । आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः ॥ ९ ॥
translation: The passionate desire foods that are bitter, sour, saline, over-hot, pungent, dry and burning and which produce pain, grief and sickness.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् । उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥ १० ॥
translation: That which is stale and flat, putrid and corrupt, leavings also and unclean, is the food dear to the dark.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टोय इज्यते । यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥ ११ ॥
translation: The sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for fruit, as enjoined by the ordinances, under the firm belief that sacrifice is a duty, that is pure.
