chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् । इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥ १२ ॥
translation: The sacrifice offered with a view verily to fruit, and also indeed for self-glorification, O best of the Bhâratas; know thou that to be of passion.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् । श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥ १३ ॥
translation: The sacrifice contrary to the ordinances, without distributing food, devoid of words of power and without gifts, empty of faith, is said to be of darkness.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् । ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥ १४ ॥
translation: Worship given to the Gods, to the twice-born, to the teachers and to the wise, purity, straightforwardness, continence and harmlessness, are called the austerity of the body.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Speech causing no annoyance, truthful, pleasant and beneficial, the practice of the study of the Scriptures, are called the austerity of speech.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः । भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥ १६ ॥
translation: Mental happiness, equilibrium, silence, self-control, purity of nature—these are called the austerity of the mind.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः । अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥ १७ ॥
translation: This threefold austerity, performed by men with the utmost faith, without desire for fruit, harmonised, is said to be pure.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् । क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥ १८ ॥
translation: The austerity which is practised with the object of gaining respect, honour and worship, and for ostentation, is said to be of passion, unstable and fleeting.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः । परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ १९ ॥
translation: That austerity done under a deluded understanding, with self-torture, or with the object of destroying another, that is declared of darkness.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे । देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥ २० ॥
translation: That alms given to one who does nothing in return, believing that a gift ought to be made in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that alms is accounted pure.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः । दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥ २१ ॥
translation: That given with a view to receiving in return, or looking for fruit again, or grudgingly, that alms is accounted of passion.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते । असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २२ ॥
translation: That alms given at unfit place and time, and to unworthy persons, disrespectfully and contemptuously, that is declared of darkness.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: ओं तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः । ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥ २३ ॥
translation: "Aum Tat Sat," this has been considered to be the threefold designation of the Eternal. By that were ordained of old Brâhmanas, Vedas and sacrifices.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः । प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥ २४ ॥
translation: Therefore with the pronunciation of "Aum" the acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity as laid down in the ordinances are always commenced by the knowers of the Eternal.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः । दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥ २५ ॥
translation: With the pronunciation of "Tat" and without aiming at fruit are performed the various acts of sacrifice, austerity and gift, by those desiring liberation.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते । प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥ २६ ॥
translation: "Sat" is used in the sense of reality and goodness; likewise, O Pârtha, the word "Sat" is used in the sense of a good work.

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते । कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and gift is also called "Sat", and action for the sake of the Supreme is also named "Sat."

chapterSummary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.
sanskrit: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् । असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥ २८ ॥
translation: Whatsoever is wrought without faith, oblation, gift, austerity, or other deed, "Asat" it is called, O Pârtha; it is nought, here or hereafter.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् । त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन ॥ १ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: I desire, O mighty-armed, to know severally the essence of renunciation, O Hrishîkesha, and of relinquishment, O Keshinishûdana.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः ॥ २ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Sages have known as renunciation the renouncing of works with desire; the relinquishing of the fruit of all actions is called relinquishment by the wise.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः । यज्ञदानतपः कर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे ॥ ३ ॥
translation: "Action should be relinquished as an evil," declare some thoughtful men; "acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinquished," say others.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम । त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः सम्प्रकीर्तितः ॥ ४ ॥
translation: Hear my conclusions as to that relinquishment, O best of the Bhâratas; since relinquishment, O tiger of men, has been explained as threefold.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यज्ञदानतपः कर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् । यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् ॥ ५ ॥
translation: Acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinquished, but should be performed; sacrifice, gift and also austerity are the purifiers of the intelligent.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च । कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम् ॥ ६ ॥
translation: But even these actions should be done leaving aside attachment and fruit, O Pârtha; that is my certain and best belief.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते । मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः ॥ ७ ॥
translation: Verily renunciation of actions that are prescribed is not proper; the relinquishment thereof from delusion is said to be of darkness.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् । स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥ ८ ॥
translation: He who relinquisheth an action from fear of physical suffering, saying "Painful," thus performing a passionate relinquishment, obtaineth not the fruit of relinquishment.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन । सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥ ९ ॥
translation: He who performeth a prescribed action, saying, "it ought to be done," O Arjuna, relinquishing attachment and also fruit, that relinquishment is regarded as pure.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते । त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥ १० ॥
translation: The relinquisher pervaded by purity, intelligent and with doubts cut away, hateth not unpleasurable action nor is attached to pleasurable.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः । यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥ ११ ॥
translation: Nor indeed can embodied beings completely relinquish action; verily he who relinquisheth the fruit of action, he is said to be a relinquisher.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् । भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥ १२ ॥
translation: Good, evil and mixed—threefold is the fruit of action hereafter for the non-relinquisher; but there is none ever for the renouncer.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे । साङ्ख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥ १३ ॥
translation: These five causes, O mighty-armed, learn of Me as declared in the Sâñkhya system for the accomplishment of all actions:

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् । विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥ १४ ॥
translation: The body, the actor, the various organs, the diverse kinds of energies, and the presiding deities also, the fifth.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: शरीरवाङ्‌मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः । न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥ १५ ॥
translation: Whatever action a man performeth by his body, speech and mind, whether right or the reverse, these five are the cause thereof.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥ १६ ॥
translation: That being so, he verily who—owing to untrained Reason—looketh on his Self, which is isolated, as the actor, he of perverted intelligence, seeth not.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते । हत्वाऽपि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥ १७ ॥
translation: He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose Reason is not affected, though he slay these peoples, he slayeth not, nor is bound.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना । करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसङ्ग्रहः ॥ १८ ॥
translation: Knowledge, the knowable and the knower, the threefold impulse to action; the organ, the action, the actor, the threefold constituents of action.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः । प्रोच्यते गुणसङ्ख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि ॥ १९ ॥
translation: Knowledge, action and actor in the category of qualities are also said to be severally threefold, from the difference of qualities; hear thou duly these also.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते । अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥ २० ॥
translation: That by which one indestructible Being is seen in all beings, inseparate in the separated, know thou that knowledge as pure.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् । वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥ २१ ॥
translation: But that knowledge which regardeth the several manifold existences in all beings as separate, that knowledge know thou as of passion;

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन् कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् । अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २२ ॥
translation: While that which clingeth to each one thing as if it were the whole, without reason, without grasping the reality, narrow, that is declared to be dark.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् । अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥ २३ ॥
translation: An action which is ordained, done by one undesirous of fruit, devoid of attachment, without love or hate, that is called pure.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः । क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २४ ॥
translation: But that action that is done by one longing for desires, or again with egoism, or with much effort, that is declared to be passionate.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् । मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥ २५ ॥
translation: The action undertaken from delusion, without regard to capacity and consequences—loss and injury to others—that is declared to be dark.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्त्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥ २६ ॥
translation: Liberated from attachment, not egoistic, endued with firmness and confidence, unchanged by success or failure, that actor is called pure.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः । हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥ २७ ॥
translation: Impassioned, desiring to obtain the fruit of actions, greedy, harmful, impure, moved by joy and sorrow, such an actor is pronounced passionate.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः । विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥ २८ ॥
translation: Discordant, vulgar, stubborn, cheating, malicious, indolent, despairful, procrastinating, that actor is called dark.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु । प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय ॥ २९ ॥
translation: The division of Reason and of firmness also, threefold according to the qualities, hear thou related, unreservedly and severally, O Dhananjaya.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये । बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥ ३० ॥
translation: That which knoweth energy and abstinence, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation, that Reason is pure, O Pârtha.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च । अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥ ३१ ॥
translation: That by which one understandeth away Right and Wrong and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, that Reason, O Pârtha, is passionate.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसा वृता । सर्वार्थान् विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥ ३२ ॥
translation: That which, enwrapped in darkness, thinketh wrong to be right and seeth all things subverted, that Reason, O Pârtha, is of darkness. 32)

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः । योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥ ३३ ॥
translation: The unwavering firmness by which, through Yoga, one restraineth the activity of the mind, of the life breaths and of the sense-organs, that firmness, O Pârtha, is pure.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन । प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥ ३४ ॥
translation: But the firmness, O Arjuna, by which, from attachment desirous of fruit, one holdeth fast duty, desire and wealth, that firmness, O Pârtha, is passionate.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च । न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥ ३५ ॥
translation: That by which one from stupidity doth not abandon sleep, fear, grief, despair, and also vanity, that firmness, O Pârtha, is dark.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ । अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥ ३६ ॥
translation: And now the threefold kinds of pleasure hear thou from Me, O bull of the Bhâratas. That in which one by practice rejoiceth, and which putteth an end to pain;

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् । तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥ ३७ ॥
translation: Which at first is as venom but in the end is as nectar; that pleasure is said to be pure, born of the blissful knowledge of the Self.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् । परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥ ३८ ॥
translation: That which from the union of the senses with their objects at first is as nectar, but in the end is like venom, that pleasure is accounted passionate.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः । निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ ३९ ॥
translation: That pleasure which both at first and afterwards is delusive of the self, arising from sleep, indolence and heedlessness, that is declared dark.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः । सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः ॥ ४० ॥
translation: There is not an entity, either on the earth or again in heaven among the Shining Ones, that is liberated from these three qualities, born of Matter.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप । कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः ॥ ४१ ॥
translation: Of Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaishyas and Shûdras, O Parantapa, the duties have been distributed, according to the qualities born of their own natures.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च । ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥ ४२ ॥
translation: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness and also uprightness, wisdom, knowledge, belief in God, are the Brâhmana duty, born of his own nature.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् । दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥ ४३ ॥
translation: Prowess, splendour, firmness, dexterity, and also not flying from battle, generosity, the nature of a ruler, are the Kshattriya duty, born of his own nature.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् । परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥ ४४ ॥
translation: Ploughing, protection of kine, and trade are the Vaishya duty, born of his own nature. Action of the nature of service is the Shûdra duty, born of his own nature.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः । स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥ ४५ ॥
translation: Man reacheth perfection by each being intent on his own duty. Listen thou how perfection is won by him who is intent on his own duty.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥ ४६ ॥
translation: He from whom is the emanation of beings, by Whom all This is pervaded, by worshipping Him in his own duty a man winneth perfection.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: श्रेयान् स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ ४७ ॥
translation: Better is one's own duty though destitute of merits than the well-executed duty of another. He who doeth the duty laid down by his own nature incurreth not sin.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥ ४८ ॥
translation: Congenital duty, O son of Kunti, though defective, ought not to be abandoned. All undertakings indeed are clouded by defects as fire by smoke.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः । नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥ ४९ ॥
translation: He whose Reason is everywhere unattached, the self-subdued, dead to desires, he goeth by renunciation to the supreme perfection of freedom from obligation.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाऽऽप्नोति निबोध मे । समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥ ५० ॥
translation: How he who hath attained perfection obtaineth the Eternal, that highest state of wisdom, learn thou from Me only succinctly, O Kaunteya.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियस्य च । शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥ ५१ ॥
translation: United to this Reason, purified, controlling the self by firmness, having abandoned sound and the other objects of the senses, having laid aside passion and malice,

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः । ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥ ५२ ॥
translation: Dwelling in solitude, abstemious, speech, body and mind subdued, constantly fixed in meditation and yoga, taking refuge in dispassion,

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् । विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥ ५३ ॥
translation: Having cast aside egoism, violence, arrogance, desire, wrath, covetousness, selfless and peaceful—he is fit to become the Eternal.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥ ५४ ॥
translation: Becoming the Eternal, serene in the Self, he neither grieveth nor desireth; the same to all beings, he obtaineth supreme devotion unto Me.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः । ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥ ५५ ॥
translation: By devotion he knoweth Me in essence, who and what I am; having thus known Me in essence he forthwith entereth into the Supreme.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः । मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥ ५६ ॥
translation: Though ever performing all actions, taking refuge in Me, by My grace he obtaineth the eternal indestructible abode.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः । बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥ ५७ ॥
translation: Renouncing mentally all works in Me, intent on Me, resorting to the yoga of discrimination, have thy thought ever on Me.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि । अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥ ५८ ॥
translation: Thinking on Me, thou shalt overcome all obstacles by My grace: but if from egoism thou wilt not listen, thou shalt be destroyed utterly.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे । मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥ ५९ ॥
translation: Entrenched in egoism, thou thinkest, "I will not fight;" to no purpose thy determination; nature will constrain thee.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा । कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥ ६० ॥
translation: O son of Kuntî, bound by thine own duty born of thine own nature, that which from delusion thou desirest not to do, even that helplessly thou shalt perform.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति । भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥ ६१ ॥
translation: The Lord dwelleth in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, by His illusive Power causing all beings to revolve, as though mounted on a potter's wheel.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत । तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥ ६२ ॥
translation: Flee unto Him for shelter with all thy being, O Bhârata; by His grace thou shalt obtain supreme peace, the everlasting dwelling-place.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्‌गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥ ६३ ॥
translation: Thus hath wisdom, more secret than secrecy itself, been declared unto thee by Me; having reflected on it fully, then act thou as thou listest.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥ ६४ ॥
translation: Listen thou again to My supreme word, most secret of all; beloved art thou of Me, and steadfast of heart, therefore will I speak for thy benefit.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥ ६५ ॥
translation: Merge thy mind in Me, be my devotee, sacrifice to Me, prostrate thyself before Me, thou shalt come even to Me. I pledge thee My troth; thou art dear to Me.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज । अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥ ६६ ॥
translation: Abandoning all duties come unto Me alone for shelter; sorrow not, I will liberate thee from all sins.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन । न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥ ६७ ॥
translation: Never is this to be spoken by thee to anyone who is without asceticism, nor without devotion, nor to one who desireth not to listen, nor yet to him who speaketh evil of Me.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: य इदं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति । भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयम् ॥ ६८ ॥
translation: He who shall declare this supreme secret among My devotees, having shown the highest devotion for Me, without doubt he shall come to Me.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः । भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥ ६९ ॥
translation: Nor is there any among men who performeth dearer service to Me than he, nor any other shall be more beloved by Me on earth than he.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः । ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥ ७० ॥
translation: And he who shall study this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall be worshipped with the sacrifice of wisdom. Such is My mind.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः । सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभांल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥ ७१ ॥
translation: The man also who, full of faith, merely heareth it unreviling, even he, freed from evil, obtaineth the radiant worlds of the righteous.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा । कच्चिदज्ञानसम्मोहः प्रणष्टस्ते धनञ्जय ॥ ७२ ॥
translation: Hath this been heard, O son of Prithâ, with one-pointed mind? Has thy delusion, caused by unwisdom, been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । नष्टो मोहः स्मूतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाऽच्युत । स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥ ७३ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Destroyed is my delusion. I have gained knowledge through Thy grace, O Immutable one. I am firm, my doubts have fled away. I will do according to Thy word.

translation: Sanjaya said: I heard this marvellous dialogue of Vâsudeva, and of the great-souled Partha, causing my hair to stand on end.

translation: By the favour of Vyâsa I listened to this secret and supreme yoga from the Lord of Yoga, Krishna Himself, speaking before mine eyes.

chapterSummary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. translation: O King, remembering, remembering this marvellous and holy dialogue between Keshava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

translation: Remembering, remembering, also that most marvellous form of Hari, great is my wonder, O King. I rejoice, again and again.

sanskrit: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः । तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥ ७८ ॥
translation: Wherever is Krishna, Yoga's Lord, wherever is Pârtha, the archer, assured are there prosperity, victory and happiness. So I think.
